title.en: Volume 168 Biographies 93: Wang Zhiyi, Wang Shuwen and Relative: Wang Pi, Lu Zhi, Liu Yuxi, Liu Zongyuan, Cheng Yi

sentences.zh: 韋執誼，京兆舊族也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhiyi was of an old clan from Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyi belonged to an established family of the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 幼有才。

translations.literal: From youth he had talent.
translations.idiomatic: He showed talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，對策異等，授右拾遺。

translations.literal: Upon attaining jinshi rank, his policy response was graded exceptional, and he was appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination with an outstanding policy essay, he was made Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 年逾冠，入翰林為學士，便敏側媚，得幸于德宗。

translations.literal: Before he was much past twenty, he entered the Hanlin as academician, quick-witted and ingratiating, and won Emperor Dezong's favor.
translations.idiomatic: While still barely past his coming-of-age, he entered the Hanlin Academy as an academician. Quick and obsequious, he won the favor of Emperor Dezong.

sentences.zh: 使豫詩歌屬和，被詔稱旨。

translations.literal: He was made to take part in composing poems in reply to the emperor's, and by imperial edict was praised as pleasing to the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him join in poetic exchanges, and an edict declared that his verses matched the imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 與裴延齡、韋渠牟等寵相埒，出入備顧問。

translations.literal: His favored status equaled that of Pei Yanling, Wei Qumou, and the like; he went in and out as an attendant counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He stood among the emperor's favorites on par with Pei Yanling and Wei Qumou, attending the throne as a trusted adviser.

sentences.zh: 帝誕日，皇太子獻畫浮屠象，帝使執誼贊之，太子賜以帛，詔執誼到東宮謝。

translations.literal: On the emperor's birthday, the crown prince presented painted images of Buddhist figures; the emperor had Zhiyi compose praise for them; the crown prince rewarded him with silk, and an edict ordered Zhiyi to go to the Eastern Palace to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's birthday the crown prince offered painted Buddhist icons. The emperor had Zhiyi write laudatory verses; the prince rewarded him with silk and ordered him to the Eastern Palace to express thanks.

sentences.zh: 太子卒見無所藉言者，乃曰：「君知王叔文乎？

translations.literal: When the crown prince suddenly saw him and had no pretext for conversation, he said, "Do you know Wang Shuwen?
translations.idiomatic: Caught off guard with nothing else to discuss, the crown prince asked, "Do you know Wang Shuwen?

sentences.zh: 美才也。」

translations.literal: A man of fine talent.
translations.idiomatic: He is a man of exceptional ability.

sentences.zh: 執誼繇是與叔文善。

translations.literal: From this Zhiyi became friendly with Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: From that meeting Zhiyi and Shuwen became close.

sentences.zh: 以母喪解。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 終喪，為吏部郎中，數召至禁中。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became Director in the Ministry of Personnel and was repeatedly summoned to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel and was often summoned to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 補闕張正一以上書召見，所善王仲舒、韋成季、劉伯芻、裴愬、常仲孺、呂洞往賀之，或謂執誼曰：「彼將論君與叔文鉤党事。」

translations.literal: Supplementer Zhang Zhengyi and others were summoned after submitting memorials; Zhiyi's friends Wang Zhongshu, Wei Chengji, Liu Bochou, Pei Su, Chang Zhongru, and Lü Dong went to congratulate them. Someone told Zhiyi, "They will discuss your factional ties with Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Supplementer Zhang Zhengyi and others had been summoned after submitting memorials, and Zhiyi's friends Wang Zhongshu, Wei Chengji, Liu Bochou, Pei Su, Chang Zhongru, and Lü Dong went to congratulate them. Someone warned Zhiyi, "They mean to raise your clique with Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 執誼即白成季等朋比，有所窺望。

translations.literal: Zhiyi immediately reported that Chengji and the others were banding together with ulterior designs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi at once informed on Chengji and the rest as forming a clique with hidden ambitions.

sentences.zh: 帝詔金吾伺，得相過食飲狀，悉逐出之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Imperial Guard to watch; when evidence was obtained of their meeting to eat and drink together, all were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Imperial Guard to investigate; once their gatherings for meals were confirmed, all were driven out.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，以疾不親政，叔文用事，乃擢執誼為尚書左丞、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, he did not personally govern because of illness; Shuwen held power, and Zhiyi was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, illness kept him from governing in person; with Shuwen in control, Zhiyi was elevated to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 叔文與王稻居中竊命，欲執誼據以奉行，因用迷奪朝權。

translations.literal: Shuwen and Wang Pi held secret authority from within the palace; they wanted Zhiyi to rely on them in carrying out orders, and by this means confusedly seized court power.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen and Wang Pi wielded secret authority from within the palace. They intended Zhiyi to execute their will, and through this confusion they usurped control of the court.

sentences.zh: 執誼既為所引，然外迫公議，欲示天下非黨與者，乃時時異論相可否，而密謝叔文曰：「不敢負約，欲共濟國家事爾。」

translations.literal: Although Zhiyi had been drawn in by them, public opinion pressed him from outside; wishing to show the world he was no partisan, he would now and then dispute points pro and con, yet secretly apologized to Shuwen, saying, "I dare not break our agreement — I only wish to work together for the affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhiyi had been brought in by them, public opinion constrained him from outside. To show the world he was no faction man, he would occasionally argue one way or another in council, yet secretly assured Shuwen, "I do not mean to break our pact — I only want us to serve the realm together.

sentences.zh: 叔文數為所梗，遂詬怒，反成仇怨。

translations.literal: Shuwen was repeatedly obstructed by him, grew abusive and angry, and they became enemies instead.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was thwarted by him again and again, flew into rage and recrimination, and they turned into bitter foes.

sentences.zh: 及憲宗受內禪，流叔文、伾，分北支黨，貶執誼為崖州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong received the inner abdication, Shuwen and Pi were exiled, the northern branch of the faction was broken up, and Zhiyi was demoted to Registrar of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne through the inner abdication, Shuwen and Pi were banished, the northern wing of the faction was dispersed, and Zhiyi was demoted to Registrar of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 帝以宰相杜黃裳之婿，故最後貶。

translations.literal: Because he was the son-in-law of Chancellor Du Huangshang, the emperor demoted him last.
translations.idiomatic: As the son-in-law of Chancellor Du Huangshang, he was the last to be demoted.

sentences.zh: 執誼已失形勢，知禍且及，雖尚在位，而臨事奄奄無氣，聞人足聲輒悸動，至於敗。

translations.literal: Zhiyi had already lost his position of strength, knew disaster was near, and though still in office, when facing affairs he was feeble and spiritless; at the sound of footsteps he would start in fright — until his fall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi had already lost his footing and knew ruin was coming. Though still in office, he handled affairs without vigor and trembled at every footfall — until the end.

sentences.zh: 始未顯時，不喜人言嶺南州縣。

translations.literal: Before he rose to prominence, he disliked hearing people speak of the prefectures and counties of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Before he rose to prominence, he could not bear to hear anyone mention the prefectures of the far south.

sentences.zh: 既為郎，嘗詣職方觀圖，至嶺南輒瞑目，命左右徹去。

translations.literal: After he became a court gentleman, he once went to the Bureau of Appointments to view maps; whenever he reached Lingnan he would shut his eyes and order his attendants to remove the section.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became a court gentleman, he visited the Bureau of Appointments to view maps; whenever the scroll reached Lingnan he shut his eyes and had his attendants roll it away.

sentences.zh: 及為相，所坐堂有圖，不就省。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor, there was a map in the hall where he sat, and he would not enter to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: After he became chancellor, a map hung in his hall of office, and he refused to go in and look at it.

sentences.zh: 既易旬，試觀之，崖州圖也，以為不祥，惡之。

translations.literal: After some ten days had passed, he tried to look at it — it was a map of Yazhou; he took it as an ill omen and hated it.
translations.idiomatic: After about ten days he tried to look — it was a map of Yazhou. He took it as a bad omen and loathed it.

sentences.zh: 果貶死。

translations.literal: In the end he was demoted and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was indeed demoted there and died.

sentences.zh: 王叔文，越州山陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen was a native of Shanyin in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen was a native of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以棋待詔。

translations.literal: He served as chess attendant awaiting imperial summons.
translations.idiomatic: He served at court as a chess attendant awaiting imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 頗讀書，班班言治道。

translations.literal: He read considerably and spoke clearly and at length on the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and spoke with evident learning on matters of governance.

sentences.zh: 德宗詔直東宮，太子引以侍讀，因論政及宮市之弊。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong ordered him assigned to the Eastern Palace; the crown prince brought him in as reading companion, and they discussed governance and the abuses of the palace market.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong assigned him to the Eastern Palace; the crown prince took him on as reading companion, and they discussed statecraft and the abuses of the palace market.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「寡人見上，將極言之。」

translations.literal: The crown prince said, "When I see my father, I shall speak out to the full.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "When I see my father, I shall speak my mind fully.

sentences.zh: 坐皆趣贊，叔文獨嘿然。

translations.literal: All present hastened to approve; Shuwen alone remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present rushed to agree; only Shuwen stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 既罷，太子曰：「向君無言，何哉？」

translations.literal: When the meeting ended, the crown prince said, "Just now you said nothing — why?
translations.idiomatic: When they adjourned, the crown prince asked, "You said nothing just now — why?

sentences.zh: 叔文曰：「太子之事上，非視膳問安無與也。

translations.literal: Shuwen said, "In serving his father, the crown prince has no business beyond attending meals and inquiring after his health.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen replied, "A crown prince's duty to his father is not to go beyond attending meals and asking after his health.

sentences.zh: 且陛下在位久，有如小人間之，謂殿下收厭群情，則安解乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, His Majesty has reigned long; if petty men should sow discord and say that Your Highness is currying favor with the multitude, how would you explain yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the emperor has reigned for many years. If petty men should whisper that Your Highness is courting popular favor, how would you answer?"

sentences.zh: 太子謝曰：「非先生不聞此言！」

translations.literal: The crown prince apologized, saying, "Had it not been for you, Sir, I would never have heard this!"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince thanked him: "But for you, Sir, I would never have heard this!"

sentences.zh: 繇是重之，宮中事鹹與參訂。

translations.literal: From this he valued him highly, and all palace affairs were discussed and decided with his participation.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the prince held him in high regard, and Shuwen was consulted on all palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 叔文淺中浮表，遂肆言不疑，曰：「某可為相，某可為將，它日幸用之。」

translations.literal: Shuwen was shallow within and showy without; he then spoke freely without reserve, saying, "So-and-so can be chancellor, so-and-so can be general — when the time comes I shall gladly employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was shallow in mind and flashy in manner. He began to speak without restraint: "This man can be chancellor, that one a general — when the day comes I shall put them to use.

sentences.zh: 陰結天下有名士，而士之欲速進者，率諧附之，若韋執誼、陸質、呂溫、李景儉、韓曄、韓泰、陳諫、柳宗元、劉禹錫為死友，而淩准、程又因其黨進，出入詭秘，外莫得其端。

translations.literal: Secretly he allied with famous men throughout the realm; scholars eager for rapid advancement generally attached themselves to him. Wei Zhiyi, Lu Zhi, Lü Wen, Li Jingjian, Han Ye, Han Tai, Chen Jian, Liu Zongyuan, and Liu Yuxi were sworn friends; Ling Zhun and Cheng Yi also advanced through the faction. Their comings and goings were secret and strange, and outsiders could not fathom their designs.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly cultivated ties with celebrated men across the empire, and scholars eager for quick promotion flocked to him. Wei Zhiyi, Lu Zhi, Lü Wen, Li Jingjian, Han Ye, Han Tai, Chen Jian, Liu Zongyuan, and Liu Yuxi were his closest allies; Ling Zhun and Cheng Yi also rose through the clique. Their movements were furtive and mysterious, and outsiders could not trace their purpose.

sentences.zh: 強籓劇帥，或陰相賂遺以自結。

translations.literal: Powerful frontier lords and formidable commanders sometimes secretly sent gifts to bind themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful regional lords and formidable military governors sometimes sent secret gifts to win his favor.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，不能聽政，深居施幄坐，以牛昭容、宦人李忠言侍側，群臣奏事，從幄中可其奏。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne, he could not attend to governance; he dwelt deep within, seated behind a curtain, with Lady Niu Zhaorong and the eunuch Li Zhongyan attending at his side. When ministers presented business, approval came from within the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong came to the throne he could not govern in person. He remained deep within the palace, seated behind a curtain, with Lady Niu Zhaorong and the eunuch Li Zhongyan at his side. Ministers presented business, and assent came from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 王伾密語諸黃門：「陛下素厚叔文。」

translations.literal: Wang Pi secretly told the palace eunuchs, "His Majesty has always favored Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi whispered to the palace eunuchs, "His Majesty has always held Shuwen in high regard.

sentences.zh: 即繇蘇州司功參軍拜起居郎、翰林學士。

translations.literal: Thereupon, from Registrar of Suzhou he was appointed Master of Ceremonies and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was promoted from Registrar of Suzhou to Master of Ceremonies and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 大抵叔文因伾，伾因忠言，忠言因昭容，更相依仗。

translations.literal: In general Shuwen relied on Pi, Pi relied on Zhongyan, and Zhongyan relied on Zhaorong — each leaning on the next.
translations.idiomatic: In effect Shuwen relied on Pi, Pi on Zhongyan, and Zhongyan on Zhaorong — a chain of mutual dependence.

sentences.zh: 伾主傳受，叔文主裁可，乃授之中書，執誼作詔文施行焉。

translations.literal: Pi handled transmission, Shuwen handled approval; then it was handed to the Secretariat, and Zhiyi drafted the edicts for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Pi relayed the orders, Shuwen decided what to approve, and the drafts went to the Secretariat, where Zhiyi wrote the edicts that were then issued.

sentences.zh: 時景儉居親喪，溫使吐蕃，惟質、泰、諫、准、畢、宗元、禹錫等倡譽之，以為伊、周、管、葛復出，憪然謂天下無人。

translations.literal: At the time Jingjian was in mourning for a parent, Wen was on mission to Tibet; only Zhi, Tai, Jian, Zhun, Bi, Zongyuan, Yuxi, and the rest sang his praises, declaring that Yi Yin, the Duke of Zhou, Guan Zhong, and Zhuge Liang had returned, and complacently believing no one in the realm could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjian was then in mourning, and Wen was on mission to Tibet; Zhi, Tai, Jian, Zhun, Bi, Zongyuan, Yuxi, and the rest proclaimed him a reborn Yi Yin, Duke of Zhou, Guan Zhong, or Zhuge Liang, and smugly thought the world held no equal.

sentences.zh: 叔文每言：「錢穀者，國大本，操其柄，可因以市士。」

translations.literal: Shuwen often said, "Revenue and grain are the great foundation of the state; grasping their control, one can thereby win over men.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen often said, "Finance and grain are the foundation of the state. Hold their reins and you can buy men's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 乃白用杜佑領度支、鹽鐵使，己副之，實專其政。

translations.literal: He therefore proposed that Du You head the offices of Revenue and Salt and Iron while he served as deputy — in fact monopolizing the administration.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore had Du You appointed head of the Revenue and Salt and Iron offices while he served as deputy, in reality controlling the administration himself.

sentences.zh: 不淹時，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 宦人俱文珍忌其權，罷叔文學士。

translations.literal: The eunuch Ju Wenzhen resented his power and removed Shuwen from the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Ju Wenzhen, jealous of his authority, stripped Shuwen of his Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 詔出，駭悵曰：「吾當數至此議事。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, he was alarmed and aggrieved, saying, "I ought to come here often to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict appeared, he was shocked and aggrieved: "I ought to come here regularly to discuss affairs.

sentences.zh: 不然，無繇入禁中。」

translations.literal: Otherwise there is no way to enter the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I have no way into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 伾復力請，乃聽三五日一至翰林，然不得舊職矣。

translations.literal: Pi again pressed hard, and he was allowed to come to the Hanlin once every three or five days — but he no longer held his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Pi pressed the point again, and Shuwen was allowed to visit the Hanlin every few days — but without his former title.

sentences.zh: 在省不事所職，日引其黨謀取神策兵，制天下之命。

translations.literal: At the ministry he neglected his duties, daily gathering his faction to plot seizing control of the Shence Army and commanding the fate of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At the ministry he neglected his duties, daily gathering his clique to plot taking the Shence Army and commanding the empire's fate.

sentences.zh: 乃以宿將范希朝為西北諸鎮行營兵馬使，泰為司馬副之。

translations.literal: He then appointed the veteran general Fan Xichao commander of the mobile camp armies of the northwestern circuits, with Tai as vice commander assisting him.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed the veteran general Fan Xichao commander of the northwestern circuits' mobile armies, with Tai as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 於是諸將移書中尉，告且去，宦人始悟奪其權，大怒曰：「吾屬必死其手！」

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals sent letters to the army supervisors saying they would soon leave; the eunuchs then realized their authority was being seized and raged, "We shall surely die at his hands!
translations.idiomatic: The generals then wrote to the army supervisors that they would soon depart. The eunuchs realized their power was being taken and raged, "We shall surely die at his hands!

sentences.zh: 乃諭諸鎮，慎毋以兵屬人。

translations.literal: They then instructed the circuits to be careful not to place troops under others' command.
translations.idiomatic: They instructed the circuits to be careful not to surrender command of their troops.

sentences.zh: 希朝、泰到奉天，諸將不至，乃還。

translations.literal: Xichao and Tai reached Fengtian, but the generals did not come, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao and Tai reached Fengtian, but no generals appeared, and they turned back.

sentences.zh: 叔文母死，匿不發，置酒翰林，忠言、文珍等皆在，裒金以餉，因揚言曰：「天子適射兔苑中，跨鞍若飛，敢異議者斬。」

translations.literal: Shuwen's mother died; he concealed it and did not announce the death. He set out wine in the Hanlin with Zhongyan, Wenzhen, and the rest present, gathered gold to give them, and proclaimed, "The Son of Heaven has just been shooting in the Rabbit Park, vaulting the saddle as if flying — whoever dares dissent shall be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuwen's mother died, he concealed the death. He held a feast in the Hanlin with Zhongyan, Wenzhen, and others present, collected gold to pay them off, and declared, "The emperor has just been hunting in the Rabbit Park, riding as if he flew — whoever dares object will be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 又自陳：「親疾病，以身任國大事，朝夕不得侍，今當請急，宜聽。

translations.literal: He also stated for himself, "My parent is ill; I have taken upon myself the great affairs of state and cannot attend day and night — now I must request leave and should be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also pleaded, "My parent is ill. I have shouldered the great affairs of state and cannot attend day and night — I must now request leave, and you should grant it.

sentences.zh: 然向之悉心戮力，難易亡所避，報天子異知爾。

translations.literal: Yet in the past I have devoted myself and exerted all my strength, never shunning difficulty or ease, repaying the Son of Heaven's extraordinary trust — that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have given my all without shirking hardship or ease, repaying the emperor's extraordinary trust — that is all.

sentences.zh: 今一去此，則百謗至，孰為吾助者？」

translations.literal: If I leave now, a hundred slanders will come — who will help me then?"
translations.idiomatic: If I leave now, a hundred slanders will follow — who then will stand by me?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「羊士諤毀短我，我將杖殺之，而執誼懦不果。

translations.literal: He also said, "Yang Shiyu slandered me; I was going to beat him to death, but the cowardly Zhiyi would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Yang Shiyu slandered me. I meant to beat him to death, but the timid Zhiyi would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 劉辟來為韋皋求三川，吾生平不識辟，便欲前執吾手，非凶人邪？

translations.literal: Liu Bi came to seek the Three Circuits for Wei Gao; I had never known Bi in my life, yet he tried to seize my hand — is that not the act of a violent man?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bi came to seek the Three Circuits for Wei Gao. I had never met him, yet he tried to grab my hand — is that not the act of a dangerous man?

sentences.zh: 掃木場將斬之，而執誼持不可。

translations.literal: I was about to execute him at the timber yard, but Zhiyi restrained me and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: I was about to execute him at the timber yard, but Zhiyi held me back.

sentences.zh: 每念失此二賊，令人悵恨。」

translations.literal: Whenever I think of letting these two villains go, it fills me with regret."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of letting those two villains escape, I am filled with regret."

sentences.zh: 又陳領度支所以興利去害者為己勞。

translations.literal: He also set forth the benefits he had brought and harms he had removed while heading the Revenue office as his own labors.
translations.idiomatic: He also recited the benefits he had brought and evils he had removed while heading the Revenue office as his own achievements.

sentences.zh: 文珍隨語詰折，叔文不得對。

translations.literal: Wenzhen rebutted him point by point as he spoke; Shuwen could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen challenged him on every point; Shuwen had no answer.

sentences.zh: 左右竊語曰：「母死已腐，方留此，將何為邪？」

translations.literal: Those nearby whispered, "His mother has been dead so long her body is decaying — yet he stays here; what is he doing?
translations.idiomatic: Those nearby whispered, "His mother's body is already decaying, yet he stays here — what is he after?

sentences.zh: 明日，乃發喪。

translations.literal: The next day he finally announced the death.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he at last announced the death.

sentences.zh: 執誼益不用其語，乃謀起復，斬執誼與不附己者，聞者恟懼。

translations.literal: Zhiyi paid even less heed to his words; Shuwen then plotted to resume office after mourning, execute Zhiyi and those who did not follow him — those who heard were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi paid him even less heed. Shuwen then plotted to leave mourning and resume office, execute Zhiyi and all who would not follow him — those who heard were terrified.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王為太子，群臣皆喜，獨叔文有憂色，誦杜甫諸葛祠詩以自況，歔欷泣下。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Guangling became crown prince, all the ministers rejoiced; only Shuwen looked troubled, reciting Du Fu's poem on Zhuge Liang's shrine to compare himself, sighing and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Guangling became crown prince, the ministers all rejoiced; only Shuwen looked troubled. He recited Du Fu's poem on Zhuge Liang's shrine as if it were his own story, sighing until tears fell.

sentences.zh: 太子已監國，貶渝州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Once the crown prince was regent, Shuwen was demoted to Registrar of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince assumed regency, Shuwen was demoted to Registrar of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，誅死。

translations.literal: The next year he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 附 王伾王伾者，杭州人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Wang Pi — Wang Pi was a native of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Wang Pi was a native of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 始以書待詔翰林，入太子宮侍書。

translations.literal: At first he served as calligraphy attendant awaiting summons in the Hanlin, and entered the crown prince's palace as calligraphy attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He first served in the Hanlin as a calligraphy attendant awaiting summons, then entered the crown prince's palace as calligraphy attendant.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，遷左散騎常侍、待詔。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne, Pi was transferred to Left Regular Attendant and attendant awaiting summons.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong came to the throne, Pi was made Left Regular Attendant and attendant awaiting summons.

sentences.zh: 伾本闒茸，貌陋，楚語，無它大志，帝褻寵之，不如叔文任氣好言事，為帝所禮。

translations.literal: Pi was originally coarse and lowly, ugly in appearance, speaking in Chu dialect, with no other great ambition; the emperor favored him familiarly, but unlike Shuwen's bold temperament and love of discussing affairs, he was not treated with ceremony by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was coarse and lowly by nature, plain-looking, speaking with a Chu accent, and without greater ambition. The emperor favored him casually, but unlike Shuwen — bold and eager to discuss affairs — Pi was not treated with formal respect.

sentences.zh: 至出處，又不及伾之無間也，叔文入止翰林，而伾至柿林院，見牛昭容等。

translations.literal: As for access, Shuwen could not match Pi's unimpeded entry: Shuwen entered only as far as the Hanlin, while Pi could reach the Persimmon Grove Court and see Lady Niu Zhaorong and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In access to the inner palace Shuwen could not match Pi's freedom: Shuwen stopped at the Hanlin, while Pi could reach the Persimmon Grove Court and see Lady Niu Zhaorong and the others.

sentences.zh: 當其党盛，門皆若沸羹，而伾尤通天下賕謝，日月不闋。

translations.literal: When the faction was at its height, their doors were like boiling stew; Pi especially received bribes and gifts from across the realm without cease, day after day.
translations.idiomatic: When the faction was at its height, their doors seethed like a boiling pot; Pi above all received bribes from across the empire without pause, day after day.

sentences.zh: 為巨櫝，裁竅以受珍，使不可出，則寢其上。

translations.literal: He made huge chests, cut openings to receive treasures so they could not be removed, and when full he slept atop them.
translations.idiomatic: He made enormous chests with openings cut to receive treasures so they could not be taken out; when a chest was full, he slept on top of it.

sentences.zh: 叔文既居喪，伾日請中人及杜佑起叔文為宰相，且總北軍，不許；

translations.literal: Once Shuwen was in mourning, Pi daily asked the eunuchs and Du You to recall Shuwen as chancellor and put him in command of the northern armies — this was not granted;
translations.idiomatic: Once Shuwen entered mourning, Pi daily petitioned the eunuchs and Du You to recall Shuwen as chancellor and place the northern armies under his command — permission was denied;

sentences.zh: 又請以威遠軍使同中書門下平章事，復不可。

translations.literal: he again asked that Shuwen be made Military Commissioner of Weiyuan Army and Associate Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat — again it was refused.
translations.idiomatic: he then asked that Shuwen be made Military Commissioner of the Weiyuan Army and Chancellor — again refused.

sentences.zh: 乃一日三表，皆不報。

translations.literal: He then submitted three memorials in one day; none received reply.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three memorials in a single day; none received answer.

sentences.zh: 憂悸，行且臥。

translations.literal: Anxious and fearful, he walked and then lay down.
translations.idiomatic: Anxious and fearful, he paced and then collapsed.

sentences.zh: 至夕，大呼曰：「吾疾作。」

translations.literal: By evening he cried out loudly, "My illness is upon me.
translations.idiomatic: By evening he cried out, "I am stricken!

sentences.zh: 輿歸第。

translations.literal: He was carried home in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: He was carried home in a litter.

sentences.zh: 貶開州司馬，死其所。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Kaizhou and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Kaizhou and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 支黨皆逐，惟質以前死免。

translations.literal: The branch of the faction was all expelled; only Zhi was spared because he had died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: The faction's members were all banished; only Lu Zhi was spared, having died earlier.

sentences.zh: 附 韓曄曄者，滉族子，有俊才。

translations.literal: Appendix: Han Ye — Ye was a clansman of Han Huang and had outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Han Ye was a relative of Han Huang and possessed outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 以司封郎中貶饒州司馬。

translations.literal: From Director in the Office of Enfeoffment he was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Director in the Office of Enfeoffment he was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 終永州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as Prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 附 陳諫諫警敏，嘗覽染署歲簿，悉能言其尺寸。

translations.literal: Appendix: Chen Jian — Jian was alert and quick-witted; once he had looked through the Dye Office's annual register, he could state all the measurements.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Chen Jian was sharp and quick. After reading the Dye Office's annual register once, he could recite every measurement.

sentences.zh: 所治，一閱籍，終身不忘。

translations.literal: Whatever he administered, one reading of the register and he never forgot it for life.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever office he held, one reading of its records and he remembered them for life.

sentences.zh: 自河中少尹貶台州司馬，終循州刺史。

translations.literal: From Junior Prefect of Hezhong he was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Taizhou and ended as Prefect of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Junior Prefect of Hezhong he was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Taizhou and ended as Prefect of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 附 凌準准，字宗一，有史學。

translations.literal: Appendix: Ling Zhun — Zhun, courtesy name Zongyi, had learning in history.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Ling Zhun, courtesy name Zongyi, was a scholar of history.

sentences.zh: 自翰林學士貶連州司馬，死於貶。

translations.literal: From Hanlin academician he was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Lianzhou and died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin academician he was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Lianzhou and died in banishment.

sentences.zh: 附 韓泰泰，字安平，有籌畫，伾、叔文所倚重，能決大事。

translations.literal: Appendix: Han Tai — Tai, courtesy name Anping, had strategic ability; Pi and Shuwen relied heavily on him, and he could decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Han Tai, courtesy name Anping, was a strategist whom Pi and Shuwen relied on heavily and who could decide weighty matters.

sentences.zh: 以戶部郎中、神策行營節度司馬貶虔州司馬。

translations.literal: From Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Adjutant of the Shence mobile camp he was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Adjutant of the Shence mobile camp he was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 終湖州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as Prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 陸質，字伯沖。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Bochong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Bochong.

sentences.zh: 七代祖澄，仕梁為名儒。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Cheng served the Liang as a celebrated Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor Cheng had served the Liang as a renowned scholar.

sentences.zh: 世居吳。

translations.literal: The family had long resided in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long lived in the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 明《春秋》，師事趙匡，匡師啖助，質盡傳二家學。

translations.literal: He mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, studied under Zhao Kuang — Kuang's teacher was Tan Zhu — and Zhi fully inherited the learning of both schools.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, studying under Zhao Kuang, whose own teacher was Tan Zhu; Zhi fully inherited the learning of both masters.

sentences.zh: 陳少遊鎮淮南，表在幕府，薦之朝，授左拾遺。

translations.literal: When Chen Shaoyou governed Huainan, he listed Zhi in his staff, recommended him to court, and Zhi was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shaoyou governed Huainan, Zhi served on his staff and was recommended to court, receiving appointment as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 累遷左司郎中，曆信、台二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Director in the Left Department and served as Prefect of Xin and Tai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director in the Left Department and served as Prefect of Xin and Tai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 質素善韋執誼，方執誼附叔文竊威柄，用其力召為給事中。

translations.literal: Zhi had long been friendly with Wei Zhiyi; just as Zhiyi was attaching himself to Shuwen and usurping authority, he used his influence to summon Zhi as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had long been close to Wei Zhiyi. When Zhiyi joined Shuwen in seizing power, he used his influence to have Zhi appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗為太子，詔侍讀。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was crown prince, an edict appointed Zhi as reading companion.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong was crown prince, an edict made Zhi his reading companion.

sentences.zh: 質本名淳，避太子名，故改。

translations.literal: Zhi's original name was Chun; to avoid the crown prince's name, it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's original name was Chun; it was changed to avoid the crown prince's taboo name.

sentences.zh: 時執誼懼太子怒己專，故以質侍東宮，陰伺意解釋左右之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhiyi feared the crown prince's anger at his monopoly of power, so he placed Zhi in the Eastern Palace to secretly watch his mood and explain matters to those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi then feared the crown prince's anger at his monopoly of power, so he placed Zhi in the Eastern Palace to watch the prince's mood and quietly explain matters to those around him.

sentences.zh: 質伺間有所言，太子輒怒曰：「陛下命先生為寡人講學，何可及它？」

translations.literal: When Zhi seized an opportunity to speak on other matters, the crown prince would angrily say, "His Majesty ordered you, Sir, to lecture me — how can you speak of anything else?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi tried to broach other subjects, the crown prince would angrily say, "His Majesty ordered you to instruct me — how can you speak of anything else?

sentences.zh: 質惶懼出。

translations.literal: Zhi would withdraw in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi would withdraw in fear.

sentences.zh: 執誼未敗時，質病甚，太子已即位，為臨問加禮。

translations.literal: Before Zhiyi's fall, Zhi was gravely ill; the crown prince had already ascended the throne and visited him in inquiry, showing him special honor.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhiyi's fall Zhi was gravely ill. The crown prince had already ascended the throne and visited him with special honor.

sentences.zh: 卒，門人以質能文聖人書，通於後世，私共諡曰文通先生。

translations.literal: When he died, his disciples, because Zhi could expound the sage's writings and communicate them to later ages, privately together posthumously styled him Master Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master Wentong, holding that he could expound the sage's writings for posterity.

sentences.zh: 所著書甚多，行於世。

translations.literal: The books he wrote were many and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote many works that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 劉禹錫，字夢得，自言系出中山。

translations.literal: Liu Yuxi, courtesy name Mengde, said of himself that his lineage descended from Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuxi, courtesy name Mengde, claimed descent from the house of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 世為儒。

translations.literal: For generations the family were Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been scholars.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，登博學宏辭科，工文章。

translations.literal: He attained jinshi rank, passed the examination in erudite learning and literary composition, and excelled at writing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and the erudite learning and literary composition exam, and excelled at prose.

sentences.zh: 淮南杜佑表管書記，入為監察御史。

translations.literal: Du You of Huainan recommended him as chief secretary; he entered court as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Du You of Huainan recommended him as chief secretary, and he entered court as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 素善韋執誼。

translations.literal: He had long been friendly with Wei Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been close to Wei Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 時王叔文得幸太子，禹錫以名重一時，與之交，叔文每稱有宰相器。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Shuwen had won the crown prince's favor; Yuxi, famed throughout the age, associated with him, and Shuwen often said he had the makings of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shuwen won the crown prince's favor, Yuxi — famed throughout the age — joined him, and Shuwen often said he had the makings of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，朝廷大議秘策多出叔文，引禹錫及柳宗元與議禁中，所言必從。

translations.literal: When the crown prince ascended the throne, most of the court's great deliberations and secret policies came from Shuwen; he brought in Yuxi and Liu Zongyuan to deliberate within the inner palace, and what they said was always followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince ascended the throne, most major policies came from Shuwen. He brought Yuxi and Liu Zongyuan into inner-palace deliberations, and their counsel was always followed.

sentences.zh: 擢屯田員外郎，判度支、鹽鐵案，頗馮藉其勢，多中傷士。

translations.literal: Yuxi was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Public Works and adjudicated the Revenue and Salt and Iron offices; relying heavily on their power, he often slandered gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Public Works and adjudicated Revenue and Salt and Iron affairs. Leaning heavily on factional power, he often slandered rivals.

sentences.zh: 若武元衡不為柳宗元所喜，自御史中丞下除太子右庶子；

translations.literal: For example, because Wu Yuanheng was disliked by Liu Zongyuan, he was demoted from Censor-in-Chief to Right Assistant to the Crown Prince;
translations.idiomatic: Because Wu Yuanheng was disliked by Liu Zongyuan, he was demoted from Censor-in-Chief to Right Assistant to the Crown Prince;

sentences.zh: 御史竇群劾禹錫挾邪亂政，群即日罷；

translations.literal: Censor Dou Qun impeached Yuxi for using wickedness to corrupt governance, and Qun was dismissed the same day;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Dou Qun impeached Yuxi for using factional intrigue to corrupt governance, and Qun was dismissed the same day;

sentences.zh: 韓皋素貴，不肯親叔文等，斥為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Han Gao was by nature proud and would not associate with Shuwen and the rest, so he was expelled as Military Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gao, proud by nature, refused to associate with Shuwen and his circle, and was sent out as Military Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 凡所進退，視愛怒重輕，人不敢指其名，號「二王、劉、柳」。

translations.literal: All appointments and dismissals depended on their likes and dislikes, heavy or light; people dared not name them directly and called them "the Two Wangs, Liu, and Liu."
translations.idiomatic: All appointments and dismissals followed their whims; people dared not name them openly and called them "the Two Wangs, Liu, and Liu."

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，叔文等敗，禹錫貶連州刺史，未至，斥朗州司馬。

translations.literal: When Xianzong ascended the throne, Shuwen and the rest fell; Yuxi was demoted to Prefect of Lianzhou, but before he arrived was further expelled as Prefectural Adjutant of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong came to the throne and Shuwen's faction fell, Yuxi was demoted to Prefect of Lianzhou; before he arrived he was further banished as Prefectural Adjutant of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 州接夜郎諸夷，風俗陋甚，家喜巫鬼，每祠，歌《竹枝》，鼓吹裴回，其聲傖佇。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered the Yelang tribes; customs were extremely crude; families delighted in shamans and ghosts; at each sacrifice they sang "Zhuzhi," with drums and pipes circling about, the sound rustic and halting.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture bordered the Yelang tribes. Customs were extremely crude; families favored shamans and spirits. At each sacrifice they sang "Zhuzhi" songs to circling drums and pipes, the tunes rustic and halting.

sentences.zh: 禹錫謂屈原居沅、湘間作《九歌》，使楚人以迎送神，乃倚其聲，作《竹枝辭》十餘篇。

translations.literal: Yuxi thought that when Qu Yuan lived between the Yuan and Xiang rivers he wrote the Nine Songs to have the people of Chu welcome and send off the spirits; accordingly he adapted their music and composed more than ten "Zhuzhi Lyrics."
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi reasoned that Qu Yuan, living between the Yuan and Xiang rivers, had written the Nine Songs so the people of Chu could welcome and send off the spirits; he adapted that music and composed more than ten "Zhuzhi Lyrics."

sentences.zh: 於是武陵夷俚悉歌之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the tribal folk of Wuling sang them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all the tribal folk of Wuling were singing them.

sentences.zh: 始，坐叔文貶者八人，憲宗欲終斥不復，乃詔雖後更赦令不得原。

translations.literal: At first eight men were demoted for association with Shuwen; Xianzong wished to banish them permanently and never restore them, and so decreed that even if later amnesties were issued, they could not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Eight men had been banished for association with Shuwen. Xianzong wished never to restore them and decreed that even future amnesties would not apply.

sentences.zh: 然宰相哀其才且困，將澡濯用之，會程异復起領運務，乃詔禹錫等悉補遠州刺史。

translations.literal: Yet the chancellor pitied their talent and hardship and meant to cleanse and employ them; it happened that Cheng Yi was restored to oversee transport affairs, and an edict ordered Yuxi and the rest all appointed to distant prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the chancellor pitied their talent and meant to rehabilitate them. When Cheng Yi was restored to oversee transport affairs, an edict appointed Yuxi and the rest to distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 而元衡方執政，諫官頗言不可用，遂罷。

translations.literal: But Yuanheng was then in power; remonstrating officials largely said they could not be used, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: But Yuanheng was then in power; remonstrating officials largely objected, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 禹錫久落魄，鬱鬱不自聊，其吐辭多諷托幽遠，作《問大鈞》、《謫九年》等賦數篇。

translations.literal: Yuxi long remained in disgrace, depressed and unable to find ease; his utterances were mostly allegorical and remote in tone, and he wrote several fu such as "Questioning the Great Balance" and "Nine Years in Banishment."
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi long remained in disgrace, depressed and restless. His writings were mostly allegorical and remote in tone, and he composed several fu including "Questioning the Great Balance" and "Nine Years in Banishment."

sentences.zh: 又敘：「張九齡為宰相，建言放臣不宜與善地，悉徙五溪不毛處。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "When Zhang Jiuling was chancellor, he proposed that exiled officials should not be given good posts and had them all moved to the barren lands of the Five Streams.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "When Zhang Jiuling was chancellor, he proposed that exiled officials should not receive good appointments and had them all moved to the barren lands of the Five Streams.

sentences.zh: 然九齡自內職出始安，有瘴癘之歎；

translations.literal: Yet Jiuling himself, leaving an inner post for Shi'an, lamented the miasma;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jiuling himself, leaving court office for Shi'an, lamented the miasmal south;

sentences.zh: 罷政事守荊州，有拘囚之思。

translations.literal: leaving government to hold Jingzhou, he felt the thought of one imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: and after leaving the chancellorship to hold Jingzhou, felt himself a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 身出遐陬，一失意不能堪，矧華人士族必致醜地，然後快意哉！

translations.literal: He himself, coming from a remote corner, could not bear one setback — how much less must a gentleman of the capital and a great clan be sent to an ugly place before he is satisfied!
translations.idiomatic: He himself, from a remote corner, could not bear one setback — must a capital gentleman of a great clan be sent to some wretched place before he is satisfied!

sentences.zh: 議者以為開元良臣，而卒無嗣，豈忮心失恕，陰責最大，雖它美莫贖邪！」

translations.literal: Commentators thought that though he was a worthy minister of the Kaiyuan era, he ended without heirs — was it not because a jealous heart lost forgiveness, and the hidden blame was greatest, so that though he had other virtues they could not redeem it?
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that though he was a worthy Kaiyuan minister, he died without heirs — was it not because a jealous heart forfeited mercy, and the hidden penalty was greatest, so that no other virtue could redeem it?

sentences.zh: 欲感諷權近，而憾不釋。

translations.literal: He meant to move and satirize those in power nearby, yet his resentment did not abate.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to move and satirize those in power, yet his resentment did not abate.

sentences.zh: 久之，召還。

translations.literal: After a long time he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 宰相欲任南省郎，而禹錫作《玄都觀看花君子》詩，語譏忿，當路者不喜，出為播州刺史。

translations.literal: The chancellor wished to appoint him to a post in the southern ministries, but Yuxi wrote the poem "Viewing Flowers at Xuandu Temple, Gentlemen," its language mocking and bitter; those in power were displeased and sent him out as Prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor wished to appoint him to a southern ministry post, but Yuxi wrote "Viewing Flowers at Xuandu Temple, Gentlemen," its language mocking and bitter. Those in power were displeased and sent him out as Prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 詔下，御史中丞裴度為言：「播極遠，猿狖所宅，禹錫母八十餘，不能往，當與其子死訣，恐傷陛下孝治，請稍內遷。」

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Censor-in-Chief Pei Du spoke on his behalf: "Bo is extremely remote, the dwelling of monkeys and gibbons; Yuxi's mother is over eighty and cannot go — she would have to bid her son a final farewell, which I fear would harm Your Majesty's governance of filial piety. I ask that he be moved somewhat inward.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Censor-in-Chief Pei Du pleaded: "Bo is extremely remote, home to monkeys and gibbons. Yuxi's mother is over eighty and cannot follow — she would have to bid her son a final farewell, which would harm Your Majesty's governance of filial piety. I ask that he be moved somewhat inward.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為人子者宜慎事，不貽親憂。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "As a son one should be careful in affairs and not bring worry to one's parent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A son should be careful in his affairs and not bring worry to his parent.

sentences.zh: 若禹錫望它人，尤不可赦。」

translations.literal: If Yuxi looks to others, that is especially unpardonable.
translations.idiomatic: If Yuxi looks to others for rescue, that is especially unpardonable.

sentences.zh: 度不敢對，帝改容曰：「朕所言，責人子事，終不欲傷其親。」

translations.literal: Du did not dare reply; the emperor changed expression and said, "What I said was to hold a son accountable — in the end I do not wish to harm his parent.
translations.idiomatic: Du did not dare reply. The emperor softened and said, "What I said was to hold a son accountable — in the end I do not wish to harm his mother.

sentences.zh: 乃易連州，又徙夔州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then changed to Lianzhou and later transferred to Prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi was then reassigned to Lianzhou and later transferred to Prefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 禹錫嘗歎天下學校廢，乃奏記宰相曰：

translations.literal: Yuxi once lamented that schools throughout the realm had fallen into ruin and submitted a memorial to the chancellor, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi once lamented the ruin of schools throughout the realm and submitted a memorial to the chancellor, saying:

sentences.zh: 言者謂天下少士，而不知養材之道，鬱堙不揚，非天不生材也。

translations.literal: Speakers say the realm lacks scholars, yet they do not know the way to nurture talent; talent is choked and not brought forth — it is not that Heaven fails to produce it.
translations.idiomatic: People say the realm lacks scholars, yet they do not know how to nurture talent. Talent is choked and never brought forth — it is not that Heaven fails to produce it.

sentences.zh: 是不耕而歎廩庾之無餘，可乎？

translations.literal: Is this not like lamenting that the granaries have no surplus without first plowing the fields — can that be right?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not like lamenting empty granaries without first plowing the fields — can that be right?

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，學舍千二百區，生徒三千餘，外夷遣子弟入附者五國。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era there were twelve hundred school buildings and more than three thousand students; five foreign states sent sons to enter and attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era there were twelve hundred school buildings and more than three thousand students; five foreign states sent sons to study at court.

sentences.zh: 今室廬圮廢，生徒衰少，非學官不振，病無貲以給也。

translations.literal: Today buildings lie in ruins, students have dwindled — it is not that school officials lack vigor, but that there are no funds to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Today the buildings lie in ruins and students have dwindled — not because school officials lack vigor, but because there are no funds to support them.

sentences.zh: 凡學官，春秋釋奠于先師，斯止辟雍、頖宮，非及天下。

translations.literal: As for school officials, the spring and autumn libation sacrifices to the former teacher were confined to the Imperial Academy and the district schools — they did not extend to the whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: School officials' spring and autumn libation sacrifices to the former teacher were confined to the Imperial Academy and district schools — they did not extend to the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 今州縣鹹以春秋上丁有事孔子廟，其禮不應古，甚非孔子意。

translations.literal: Today all prefectures and counties hold ceremonies at Confucius temples on the first ding day of spring and autumn; the rite does not accord with antiquity and is very far from Confucius's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Today all prefectures and counties hold ceremonies at Confucius temples on the first ding day of spring and autumn — a rite that does not accord with antiquity and is far from Confucius's intent.

sentences.zh: 漢初群臣起屠販，故孝惠、高後間置原廟于郡國，逮元帝時，韋玄成遂議罷之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han the ministers rose from butchers and peddlers, so between Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gao original temples were established in commanderies and kingdoms; by Emperor Yuandi's time Wei Xuancheng proposed abolishing them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han the ministers rose from butchers and peddlers, so between Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gao original temples were established in the commanderies; by Emperor Yuandi's time Wei Xuancheng proposed abolishing them.

sentences.zh: 夫子孫尚不敢違禮饗其祖，況後學師先聖道而欲違之。

translations.literal: Confucius's own descendants dared not violate ritual in feasting their ancestor — how much less should later students who take the former sage's Way as teacher wish to violate it.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's own descendants dared not violate ritual in honoring their ancestor — how much less should later students who follow the sage's Way wish to violate it.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「祭不欲數。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says, "Sacrifice should not be frequent.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, "Sacrifice should not be frequent.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「祭神如神在。」

translations.literal: It also says, "Sacrifice to the spirits as though the spirits were present."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Sacrifice to the spirits as though the spirits were present."

sentences.zh: 與其煩於薦饗，孰若行其教？

translations.literal: Rather than trouble oneself with repeated offerings, is it not better to practice his teaching?
translations.idiomatic: Rather than trouble oneself with repeated offerings, is it not better to practice his teaching?

sentences.zh: 今教頹靡，而以非禮之祀媚之，儒者所宜疾。

translations.literal: Today teaching is decadent, yet unorthodox sacrifices are used to flatter him — this is what Confucians should abhor.
translations.idiomatic: Today teaching is decadent, yet unorthodox sacrifices are used to flatter the sage — this is what Confucians should abhor.

sentences.zh: 竊觀歷代無有是事。

translations.literal: Observing privately through the dynasties, there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Looking through the dynasties, there has never been such a practice.

sentences.zh: 武德初，詔國學立周公、孔子廟，四時祭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, an edict ordered the Imperial Academy to establish temples to the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, with sacrifices in all four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude, an edict ordered the Imperial Academy to establish temples to the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, with sacrifices in all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，詔修孔子廟兗州。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, an edict ordered repair of the Confucius temple in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era, an edict ordered repair of the Confucius temple in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 後許敬宗等奏天下州縣置三獻官，其他如立社。

translations.literal: Later Xu Jingzong and others memorialized that all prefectures and counties should establish three-offering officials, with other arrangements like those for establishing altars to the soil god.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xu Jingzong and others memorialized that all prefectures and counties should establish three-offering officials, with other arrangements modeled on the soil-god altars.

sentences.zh: 玄宗與儒臣議，罷釋奠牲牢，薦酒脯。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong deliberated with Confucian officials and abolished livestock for the libation sacrifice, offering wine and dried meat instead.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong deliberated with Confucian officials and abolished livestock for the libation sacrifice, offering wine and dried meat instead.

sentences.zh: 時王孫林甫為宰相，不涉學，使御史中丞王敬從以明衣牲牢著為令，遂無有非之者。

translations.literal: At the time Li Linfu was chancellor; unversed in learning, he had Censor-in-Chief Wang Jingcong codify bright garments and livestock as regulations, and thereafter no one objected.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Linfu was chancellor. Unversed in learning, he had Censor-in-Chief Wang Jingcong codify bright garments and livestock sacrifices as regulations, and thereafter no one objected.

sentences.zh: 今夔四縣歲釋奠費十六萬，舉天下州縣歲凡費四千萬，適資三獻官飾衣裳，飴妻子，于學無補也。

translations.literal: Today the four counties of Kuizhou spend one hundred sixty thousand per year on libation sacrifices; throughout all prefectures and counties the annual total is forty million — merely supplying the three-offering officials with garments, feeding their wives and children, with no benefit to learning.
translations.idiomatic: Today Kuizhou's four counties spend one hundred sixty thousand per year on libation sacrifices; nationwide the annual total is forty million — merely clothing three-offering officials and feeding their families, with no benefit to learning.

sentences.zh: 請下禮官博士議，罷天下州縣牲牢衣幣，春秋祭如開元時，籍其資半畀所隸州，使增學校，舉半歸太學，猶不下萬計，可以營學室，具器用，豐饌食，增掌故，以備使令，儒官各加稍食，州縣進士皆立程督，則貞觀之風，粲然可復。

translations.literal: I ask that ritual officials and erudites be ordered to deliberate, that livestock and garment offerings in all prefectures and counties be abolished and spring and autumn sacrifices restored as in the Kaiyuan era; that half the funds be allotted to the governing prefecture to expand schools, and half sent to the Imperial Academy — still no less than ten thousand in total — so that schoolrooms may be built, implements provided, food made abundant, clerks increased to meet assignments, Confucian officials each given additional stipends, and jinshi candidates in prefectures and counties all placed under scheduled supervision; then the spirit of Zhenguan could brilliantly be restored.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that ritual officials and erudites deliberate, abolish livestock and garment offerings in all prefectures and counties, and restore spring and autumn sacrifices as in the Kaiyuan era. Half the saved funds should go to each governing prefecture to expand schools, and half to the Imperial Academy — still no less than ten thousand in total — to build schoolrooms, provide implements, supply food, increase clerks, give Confucian officials additional stipends, and place jinshi candidates under scheduled supervision. Then the spirit of Zhenguan could brilliantly be restored.

sentences.zh: 當時不用其言。

translations.literal: At the time his words were not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 由和州刺史入為主客郎中，復作《游玄都》詩，且言：「始謫十年，還京師，道士植桃，其盛若霞。

translations.literal: From Prefect of Hezhou he entered court as Director in the Office of Foreign Guests; he again wrote the poem "Visiting Xuandu," saying moreover, "At first, ten years in banishment; returning to the capital, Taoist priests had planted peach trees, their splendor like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: From Prefect of Hezhou he entered court as Director in the Office of Foreign Guests. He again wrote "Visiting Xuandu," saying, "Ten years in banishment; returning to the capital, Taoist priests had planted peach trees in splendor like clouds.

sentences.zh: 又十四年過之，無復一存，唯兔葵、燕麥動搖春風耳。」

translations.literal: Fourteen years later I passed there again — not one remained; only rabbit-brush and wild oats swayed in the spring wind.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen years later I passed there again — not one tree remained; only rabbit-brush and wild oats swayed in the spring wind.

sentences.zh: 以詆權近，聞者益薄其行。

translations.literal: He used this to slander those in power nearby; those who heard increasingly despised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He used this to slander those in power; those who heard increasingly despised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 俄分司東都。

translations.literal: Soon he was assigned to the eastern capital as a detached official.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned as a detached official in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴度兼集賢殿大學士，雅知禹錫，薦為禮部郎中、集賢直學士。

translations.literal: Chancellor Pei Du also served as Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; he knew Yuxi well and recommended him as Director in the Ministry of Rites and Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Pei Du, also Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, knew Yuxi well and recommended him as Director in the Ministry of Rites and Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 度罷，出為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: When Du was dismissed, Yuxi went out as Prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Du left office, Yuxi was sent out as Prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 以政最，賜金紫服。

translations.literal: For the excellence of his governance he was granted gold and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: For the excellence of his governance he was granted gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 徙汝、同二州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the two prefectures of Ru and Tong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Ru and Tong prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遷太子賓客，復分司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Mentor to the Crown Prince and again served as detached official.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Mentor to the Crown Prince and again served as a detached official.

sentences.zh: 禹錫恃才而廢，褊心不能無怨望，年益晏，偃蹇寡所合，乃以文章自適。

translations.literal: Yuxi relied on his talent yet was cast aside; narrow in heart, he could not be without resentment; as years grew late he was proud and found few companions, and so took refuge in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi relied on his talent yet was cast aside. Narrow in heart, he could not shed resentment; as he grew older he was proud and found few companions, and took refuge in writing.

sentences.zh: 素善詩，晚節尤精，與白居易酬復頗多。

translations.literal: He had always been skilled at poetry; in his later years he was especially refined, and exchanged many poems with Bai Juyi.
translations.idiomatic: He had always been skilled at poetry; in his later years he was especially refined, and exchanged many poems with Bai Juyi.

sentences.zh: 居易以詩自名者，嘗推為「詩豪」，又言：「其詩在處，應有神物護持。」

translations.literal: Juyi, who made his name through poetry, once praised him as "Poetry's Champion," and also said, "Wherever his poems are, some divine thing ought to guard them."
translations.idiomatic: Juyi, who made his name through poetry, once praised him as "Poetry's Champion," and also said, "Wherever his poems are, some divine thing ought to guard them."

sentences.zh: 會昌時，加檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he was given the additional title of Honorary Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huichang era he was given the additional title of Honorary Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-two and was posthumously granted Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two and was posthumously granted Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 始疾病，自為《子劉子傳》，稱：「漢景帝子勝，封中山，子孫為中山人。

translations.literal: When illness first came upon him, he wrote for himself "Biography of Master Liu," stating, "Emperor Jing of Han's son Sheng was enfeoffed in Zhongshan; his descendants became people of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When illness first came upon him, he wrote for himself "Biography of Master Liu," stating, "Emperor Jing of Han's son Sheng was enfeoffed in Zhongshan; his descendants became people of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 七代祖亮，元魏冀州刺史，遷洛陽，為北部都昌人，墳墓在洛北山，後其地狹不可依，乃葬滎陽檀山原。

translations.literal: My seventh-generation ancestor Liang was Regional Inspector of Ji in Northern Wei; moving to Luoyang, he became a man of Duchang in the northern district; the tombs were on Luoyang's northern hills; later the land was too narrow to rely on, so burial was made at Tanshan Plain in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: My seventh-generation ancestor Liang was Regional Inspector of Ji in Northern Wei. Moving to Luoyang, he became a man of Duchang in the northern district; the tombs were on Luoyang's northern hills, but later the land grew too narrow, so burial was made at Tanshan Plain in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 德宗棄天下，太子立，時王叔文以善弈得通籍，因間言事，積久，眾未知。

translations.literal: When Dezong abandoned the realm and the crown prince ascended, Wang Shuwen at the time, through skill at chess, gained access to the registers; he spoke on affairs in intervals; over a long time the multitude did not know.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong died and the crown prince ascended, Wang Shuwen had gained court access through skill at chess. He spoke on affairs in intervals; for a long time the court did not understand.

sentences.zh: 至起蘇州掾，超拜起居舍人、翰林學士，陰薦丞相杜佑為度支、鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: When he rose from Suzhou aide, he was abruptly promoted to Attendant of the Office of Imperial Attendants and Hanlin academician, secretly recommending Chancellor Du You as Commissioner of Revenue and Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: When he rose from Suzhou aide, he was abruptly promoted to Attendant of the Office of Imperial Attendants and Hanlin academician, secretly recommending Chancellor Du You as Commissioner of Revenue and Salt and Iron.

sentences.zh: 翌日，自為副，貴震一時。

translations.literal: The next day he made himself deputy; his eminence shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he made himself deputy; his eminence shook the court.

sentences.zh: 叔文，北海人，自言猛之後，有遠祖風，東平呂溫、隴西李景儉、河東柳宗元以為信然。

translations.literal: Shuwen was a man of Beihai; he said of himself that he was descended from Wang Meng and had the spirit of a remote ancestor; Lü Wen of Dongping, Li Jingjian of Longxi, and Liu Zongyuan of Hedong believed it true.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was from Beihai; he claimed descent from Wang Meng and the spirit of a distant forebear. Lü Wen of Dongping, Li Jingjian of Longxi, and Liu Zongyuan of Hedong believed him.

sentences.zh: 三子者皆予厚善，日夕過，言其能。

translations.literal: These three men were all close friends of mine; day and night they visited and spoke of his ability.
translations.idiomatic: These three were all close friends of mine; day and night they visited and spoke of his ability.

sentences.zh: 叔文實工言治道，能以口辯移人，既得用，所施為人不以為當。

translations.literal: Shuwen was indeed skilled at speaking on the way of governance and could move people through eloquence; once he gained employment, what he enacted people did not consider appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was indeed skilled at speaking on governance and could move people through eloquence; once in power, what he enacted people did not consider appropriate.

sentences.zh: 太上久疾，宰臣及用事者不得對，宮掖事秘，建桓立順，功歸貴臣，由是及貶。」

translations.literal: The retired emperor was long ill; chancellors and those in power could not respond; palace affairs were secret; establishing Huan and enthroning Shun — the merit went to powerful ministers; for this reason I was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor was long ill; chancellors and those in power could not respond; palace affairs were secret. Establishing Huan and enthroning Shun — the merit went to powerful ministers; for this I was demoted.

sentences.zh: 其自辯解大略如此。

translations.literal: His self-defense was broadly like this.
translations.idiomatic: His self-defense was broadly like this.

sentences.zh: 柳宗元，字子厚，其先蓋河東人。

translations.literal: Liu Zongyuan, courtesy name Zihou, his ancestors were probably people of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongyuan, courtesy name Zihou, was probably descended from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 從曾祖奭為中書令，得罪武后，死高宗時。

translations.literal: His great-great-uncle Shi was Director of the Secretariat; he offended Empress Wu and died in Gaozong's time.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-uncle Shi was Director of the Secretariat; he offended Empress Wu and died in Gaozong's reign.

sentences.zh: 父鎮，天寶末遇亂，奉母隱王屋山，常間行求養，後徙于吳。

translations.literal: His father Zhen, encountering rebellion at the end of Tianbao, took his mother to hide on Mount Wangwu, often traveling by secret paths to seek sustenance, and later moved to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen, encountering rebellion at the end of the Tianbao era, took his mother to hide on Mount Wangwu, often traveling by secret paths to seek sustenance, and later moved to Wu.

sentences.zh: 肅宗平賊，鎮上書言事，擢左衛率府兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Suzong suppressed the rebels, Zhen submitted a memorial on affairs and was promoted to Army Adjutant in the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong suppressed the rebels, Zhen submitted a memorial on state affairs and was promoted to Army Adjutant in the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 佐郭子儀朔方府，三遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He assisted Guo Ziyi in the Shuofang headquarters and was promoted three times to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Guo Ziyi at the Shuofang headquarters and was promoted three times to Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 以事觸竇參，貶夔州司馬。

translations.literal: On account of affairs he offended Dou Can and was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Dou Can over a matter and was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 還，終侍御史。

translations.literal: He returned and ended as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and ended his career as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 宗元少精敏絕倫，為文章卓偉精緻，一時輩行推仰。

translations.literal: Zongyuan from youth was keen and quick beyond compare; his writing was lofty, grand, refined, and exquisite, and men of his generation looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zongyuan was keen and quick beyond compare. His writing was lofty, grand, and exquisitely wrought, and men of his generation looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 第進士、博學宏辭科，授校書郎，調藍田尉。

translations.literal: He attained jinshi rank and passed the erudite learning and literary composition exam; he was appointed Collator and transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and erudite learning and literary composition exams, was appointed Collator, and transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 貞元十九年，為監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan he served as Acting Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan he served as Acting Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 善王叔文、韋執誼，二人者奇其才。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Wang Shuwen and Wei Zhiyi; both men marveled at his talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Wang Shuwen and Wei Zhiyi, and both men marveled at his talent.

sentences.zh: 及得政，引內禁近，與計事，擢禮部員外郎，欲大進用。

translations.literal: When they gained power, they brought him within the inner palace as an attendant and deliberated affairs with him; he was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites, with intent to advance him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When they gained power, they brought him into the inner palace as an attendant and deliberated affairs with him. He was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites, with intent to advance him further.

sentences.zh: 俄而叔文敗，貶邵州刺史，不半道，貶永州司馬。

translations.literal: Soon Shuwen fell; Zongyuan was demoted to Prefect of Shaozhou, but before half the journey was done was further demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shuwen fell. Zongyuan was demoted to Prefect of Shaozhou, but before he had gone half the journey was further banished as Prefectural Adjutant of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 既竄斥，地又荒癘，因自放山澤間，其堙厄感鬱，一寓諸文，仿《離騷》數十篇，讀者咸悲惻。

translations.literal: Once exiled, the land was also wild and miasmal; he therefore let himself go among mountains and marshes. His oppression, hardship, and melancholy he poured entirely into writing, imitating the "Li Sao" in several dozen pieces — readers all were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Once exiled to wild, miasmal country, he let himself go among mountains and marshes. His oppression and melancholy he poured entirely into writing, composing several dozen pieces in the manner of the "Li Sao" — readers were all moved to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 雅善蕭俛，詒書言情曰：

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Xiao Fu and sent him a letter expressing his feelings, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Xiao Fu and sent him a letter expressing his feelings, saying:

sentences.zh: 僕向者進當臲卼不安之勢，平居閉門，口舌無數，又久興遊者，岌岌而操其間。

translations.literal: Your servant formerly advanced amid unstable and perilous circumstances; in ordinary times I kept my doors closed, yet my words were countless, and for long there were those stirring trouble, precariously manipulating affairs between us.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant formerly advanced amid unstable and perilous circumstances. In ordinary times I kept my doors closed, yet my words were countless, and for long there were troublemakers precariously manipulating affairs between us.

sentences.zh: 其求進而退者，皆聚為仇怨，造作粉飾，蔓延益肆。

translations.literal: Those seeking advancement and those falling back all gathered as enemies, fabricating and embellishing slanders that spread ever more wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Those seeking advancement and those falling back all gathered as enemies, fabricating slanders that spread ever more wantonly.

sentences.zh: 非的然昭晰、自斷於內，孰能了僕於冥冥間哉？

translations.literal: Unless one were clearly discerning and judged within himself, who could understand your servant in the darkness?
translations.idiomatic: Unless one were clearly discerning and judged within himself, who could understand your servant in the darkness?

sentences.zh: 僕當時年三十三，自御史裏行得禮部員外郎，超取顯美，欲免世之求進者怪怒媢疾，可得乎？

translations.literal: Your servant was then thirty-three; from Acting Censor I obtained Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites, seizing a conspicuous and splendid post — could I have escaped the wonder, rage, and envy of those in the world seeking advancement?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant was then thirty-three. From Acting Censor I obtained Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites, seizing a conspicuous post — could I have escaped the wonder, rage, and envy of those seeking advancement?

sentences.zh: 與罪人交十年，官以是進，辱在附會。

translations.literal: I associated with a criminal for ten years and advanced in office thereby — the disgrace lay in attaching myself to a faction.
translations.idiomatic: I associated with a criminal for ten years and advanced in office thereby — the disgrace lay in attaching myself to a faction.

sentences.zh: 聖朝寬大，貶黜甚薄，不塞眾人之怒，謗語轉侈，囂囂嗷嗷，漸成怪人。

translations.literal: The sage dynasty is magnanimous; my demotion was very light — yet it did not stop the people's anger. Slanders grew ever more extravagant; clamor and outcry gradually made me a strange creature.
translations.idiomatic: The sage dynasty is magnanimous; my demotion was very light — yet it did not stop the people's anger. Slanders grew ever more extravagant; clamor and outcry gradually made me a strange creature.

sentences.zh: 飾智求仕者，更詈僕以悅仇人之心，日為新奇，務相悅可，自以速援引之路。

translations.literal: Those who display cleverness to seek office further reviled your servant to please the hearts of enemies, daily producing novelties, striving to please one another, thinking to speed their path to recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Those who display cleverness to seek office further reviled your servant to please our enemies, daily producing novelties and striving to please one another, thinking to speed their path to recommendation.

sentences.zh: 僕輩坐益困辱，萬罪橫生，不知其端，悲夫！

translations.literal: Your servant and his kind sat ever more trapped in disgrace; ten thousand crimes arose without knowing their source — how sad!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant and his kind sat ever more trapped in disgrace; ten thousand crimes arose without knowing their source — how sad!

sentences.zh: 人生少六七十者，今三十七矣，長來覺日月益促，歲歲更甚，大都不過數十寒暑，無此身矣。

translations.literal: Few in life reach sixty or seventy; I am now thirty-seven. As years lengthen I feel days and months grow ever shorter, each year worse than the last — in general no more than a few dozen summers and winters, and this body will be no more.
translations.idiomatic: Few in life reach sixty or seventy; I am now thirty-seven. As years lengthen I feel days and months grow ever shorter, each year worse than the last — in all, no more than a few dozen summers and winters, and this body will be no more.

sentences.zh: 是非榮辱，又何足道！

translations.literal: Right and wrong, glory and disgrace — what are they worth speaking of!
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong, glory and disgrace — what are they worth speaking of!

sentences.zh: 云云不已，祗益為罪。

translations.literal: To go on speaking thus only adds to my guilt.
translations.idiomatic: To go on speaking thus only adds to my guilt.

sentences.zh: 居蠻夷中久，慣習炎毒，昏眊重膇，意以為常。

translations.literal: Living long among barbarians, I have grown accustomed to heat and poison; dim-eyed and heavy-legged, I take it as normal.
translations.idiomatic: Living long among barbarians, I have grown accustomed to heat and poison; dim-eyed and heavy-legged, I take it as normal.

sentences.zh: 忽遇北風晨起，薄寒中體，則肌革慘懍，毛髮蕭條，瞿然注視，怵惕以為異候，意緒殆非中國人也。

translations.literal: Suddenly encountering a north wind one morning, with slight cold entering the body, then flesh and skin turn bleak and chill, hair sparse and desolate; startled I stare fixedly, fearful and alert, taking it for a strange sign — my mood is almost no longer that of a man of the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly one morning a north wind brings slight cold into the body — flesh and skin turn bleak, hair sparse and desolate. Startled, I stare fixedly, fearful and alert, taking it for a strange sign — my mood is almost no longer that of a man of the Central States.

sentences.zh: 楚、越間聲音特異，鴂舌啅噪，今聽之恬然不怪，已與為類矣。

translations.literal: Between Chu and Yue the sounds are especially strange — magpie tongues clamoring and noisy; now I hear them calmly without wonder — I have already become of their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Between Chu and Yue the sounds are especially strange — harsh tongues clamoring and noisy. Now I hear them calmly without wonder — I have already become of their kind.

sentences.zh: 家生小童，皆自然嘵嘵，晝夜滿耳；

translations.literal: The household boys born here all naturally chatter in that tongue, day and night filling the ears;
translations.idiomatic: The household boys born here all naturally chatter in that tongue, day and night filling the ears;

sentences.zh: 聞北人言，則啼呼走匿，雖病夫亦怛然駭之。

translations.literal: when they hear a northerner speak, they cry out and run to hide — even the sick are suddenly terrified by it.
translations.idiomatic: when they hear a northerner speak, they cry out and run to hide — even the sick are suddenly terrified by it.

sentences.zh: 出門見適州閭市井者，其十八九杖而後興。

translations.literal: Going out I see the townsfolk of this prefecture in the markets — eight or nine of ten lean on staffs before they can rise.
translations.idiomatic: Going out I see the townsfolk of this prefecture in the markets — eight or nine of ten lean on staffs before they can rise.

sentences.zh: 自料居此，尚復幾何，豈可更不知止，言說長短，重為一世非笑哉？

translations.literal: I reckon how long I may yet dwell here — how can I again fail to know when to stop, speaking of rights and wrongs, and again become the world's laughingstock?
translations.idiomatic: I reckon how long I may yet dwell here — how can I again fail to know when to stop, speaking of rights and wrongs, and again become the world's laughingstock?

sentences.zh: 讀《易·困卦》至「有言不信，尚口乃窮」，往復益喜，曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: Reading the "Kun" hexagram in the Changes to "Words are not believed; relying on the mouth leads to exhaustion," I read back and forth with growing delight, saying, "Alas!
