translations.idiomatic: Reading the "Kun" hexagram in the Changes to "Words are not believed; relying on the mouth leads to exhaustion," I read back and forth with growing delight, saying, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 餘雖家置一喙以自稱道，詬益甚耳。」

translations.literal: Though I kept a mouth at home to speak for myself, abuse would only grow worse.
translations.idiomatic: Though I kept a mouth at home to speak for myself, abuse would only grow worse.

sentences.zh: 用是更樂喑默，與木石為徒，不復致意。

translations.literal: For this reason I came to prefer silence, keeping company with trees and stones, no longer giving the matter thought.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason I came to prefer silence, keeping company with trees and stones, no longer giving the matter thought.

sentences.zh: 今天子興教化，定邪正，海內皆欣欣怡愉，而僕與四五子者，淪陷如此，豈非命歟？

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven raises culture and teaching, settles what is crooked and what is straight; within the seas all are joyful and content — yet your servant and four or five others have fallen so low. Is this not fate?
translations.idiomatic: Today the Son of Heaven raises culture and teaching and settles what is crooked and what is straight; within the seas all are joyful and content — yet your servant and four or five others have fallen so low. Is this not fate?

sentences.zh: 命乃天也，非云云者所制，又何恨？

translations.literal: Fate is Heaven's, not something made by all this talk — what is there to resent?
translations.idiomatic: Fate is Heaven's, not something made by all this talk — what is there to resent?

sentences.zh: 然居治平之世，終身為頑人之類，猶有少恥，未能盡忘。

translations.literal: Yet living in an age of order and peace, to spend one's whole life among obstinate men — there is still a little shame; I cannot wholly forget.
translations.idiomatic: Yet living in an age of order and peace, to spend one's whole life among obstinate men — there is still a little shame; I cannot wholly forget.

sentences.zh: 儻因賊平慶賞之際，得以見白，使受天澤餘潤，雖朽枿敗腐不能生植，猶足蒸出芝菌，以為瑞物。

translations.literal: If perchance at the time of celebrating the suppression of rebels I might be cleared and allowed to receive Heaven's remaining grace — though rotten stumps and decayed matter cannot sprout, they may still steam forth spirit fungus as an auspicious thing.
translations.idiomatic: If perchance at the time of celebrating the suppression of rebels I might be cleared and allowed to receive Heaven's remaining grace — though rotten stumps and decayed matter cannot sprout, they may still steam forth spirit fungus as an auspicious thing.

sentences.zh: 一釋廢錮，移數縣之地，則世必曰罪稍解矣。

translations.literal: Once the ban of disgrace is lifted and I am moved a few counties' distance, the world will surely say my guilt is somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ban of disgrace is lifted and I am moved a few counties' distance, the world will surely say my guilt is somewhat eased.

sentences.zh: 然後收召魂魄，買土一廛為耕氓，朝夕歌謠，使成文章，庶木鐸者採取，獻之法宮，增聖唐大雅之什，雖不得位，亦不虛為太平人矣。

translations.literal: Then I would gather back soul and spirit, buy a plot of land and a dwelling to become a farming commoner, singing day and night until it became writing — perhaps the bell-ringer would gather it and present it to the imperial court, adding to the great odes of sage Tang; though I might not hold office, I would not live the peace in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Then I would gather back soul and spirit, buy a plot of land and a dwelling to become a farming commoner, singing day and night until it became writing — perhaps the bell-ringer would gather it and present it to the imperial court, adding to the great odes of sage Tang; though I might not hold office, I would not live the peace in vain.

sentences.zh: 又詒京兆尹許孟容曰：

translations.literal: He also wrote to Metropolitan Prefect Xu Mengrong, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Metropolitan Prefect Xu Mengrong, saying:

sentences.zh: 宗元早歲與負罪者親善，始奇其能，謂可以共立仁義，裨教化。

translations.literal: Zongyuan in his early years was close to men bearing guilt; at first he marveled at their ability and thought they could together establish benevolence and righteousness and aid culture and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: In his early years Zongyuan was close to men bearing guilt. At first he marveled at their ability and thought they could together establish benevolence and righteousness and aid culture and teaching.

sentences.zh: 過不自料，勤勤勉勵，唯以忠正信義為志，興堯、舜、孔子道，利安元元為務，不知愚陋不可以強，其素意如此也。

translations.literal: Overestimating myself, I worked diligently and urged others on, taking loyalty, rectitude, faith, and righteousness as my aim, raising the Way of Yao, Shun, and Confucius, making benefit and peace for the common people my task — not knowing that stupidity and lowliness cannot be forced; such was my original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Overestimating myself, I worked diligently, taking loyalty, rectitude, faith, and righteousness as my aim, raising the Way of Yao, Shun, and Confucius and making benefit and peace for the common people my task — not knowing that stupidity and lowliness cannot be forced; such was my original intent.

sentences.zh: 末路厄塞臲卼，事既壅隔，很忤貴近，狂疏繆戾，蹈不測之辜。

translations.literal: At the end my path was blocked and perilous; affairs were already obstructed; I stubbornly offended the powerful and near; wild, careless, and perverse, I stepped into unforeseeable guilt.
translations.idiomatic: At the end my path was blocked and perilous. Affairs were obstructed; I stubbornly offended the powerful; wild, careless, and perverse, I stepped into unforeseeable guilt.

sentences.zh: 今黨與幸獲寬貸，各得善地，無公事，坐食奉祿，德至渥也。

translations.literal: Now the faction has fortunately received leniency; each has obtained a good post, no public duties, sitting and eating stipends — grace most abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Now the faction has fortunately received leniency; each has obtained a good post with no public duties, sitting and eating stipends — grace most abundant.

sentences.zh: 尚何敢更俟除棄廢痼，希望外之澤哉？

translations.literal: How would I dare still to await removal of my abandoned chronic affliction and hope for grace from outside?
translations.idiomatic: How would I dare still to await removal of my abandoned chronic affliction and hope for grace from outside?

sentences.zh: 年少氣銳，不識幾微，不知當否，但欲一心直遂，果陷刑法，皆自所求取，又何怪也？

translations.literal: Young in years, sharp in spirit, not knowing subtle signs, not knowing what was fitting — I only wished to follow my heart straight through, and indeed fell into the penal code; all was what I sought for myself — what is there to wonder at?
translations.idiomatic: Young in years, sharp in spirit, not knowing subtle signs or what was fitting — I only wished to follow my heart straight through, and indeed fell into the penal code; all was what I sought for myself — what is there to wonder at?

sentences.zh: 宗元于眾党人中，罪狀最甚，神理降罰，又不能即死，猶對人語言，飲食自活，迷不知恥，日復一日。

translations.literal: Among all the faction Zongyuan's guilt was greatest; divine principle sent down punishment, yet he could not die at once — still speaking to others, eating and drinking to keep alive, lost and knowing no shame, day after day.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the faction Zongyuan's guilt was greatest. Divine principle sent down punishment, yet he could not die at once — still speaking to others, eating and drinking to keep alive, lost and knowing no shame, day after day.

sentences.zh: 然亦有大故。

translations.literal: Yet there is also a great reason.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there is also a great reason.

sentences.zh: 自以得姓來二千五百年，代為塚嗣，今抱非常之罪，居夷獠之鄉，卑濕昏霧，恐一日填委溝壑，曠墜先緒，以是怛然痛恨，心骨沸熱。

translations.literal: Since obtaining the surname two thousand five hundred years ago, generation after generation as heirs of the ancestral tomb — now bearing extraordinary guilt, dwelling in a land of barbarians, low, damp, and dim with mist, I fear one day filling a ditch and gully, leaving the ancestral line abandoned; for this I am suddenly stricken with bitter pain, heart and bones boiling hot.
translations.idiomatic: Since obtaining the surname two thousand five hundred years ago, generation after generation as heirs of the ancestral tomb — now bearing extraordinary guilt, dwelling in a land of barbarians, low, damp, and dim with mist, I fear one day filling a ditch and gully and leaving the ancestral line abandoned; for this I am stricken with bitter pain, heart and bones boiling hot.

sentences.zh: 煢煢孤立，未有子息，荒陬中少士人女子，無與為婚，世亦不肯與罪人親昵，以是嗣續之重，不絕如縷。

translations.literal: Alone and isolated, I have no son or heir; in this wild corner there are few scholar-gentlemen's daughters, none to marry; the world also will not be intimate with a criminal — thus the weight of continuing the line hangs by a thread.
translations.idiomatic: Alone and isolated, I have no son or heir. In this wild corner there are few scholar-gentlemen's daughters to marry; the world also will not be intimate with a criminal — thus the weight of continuing the line hangs by a thread.

sentences.zh: 每春秋時饗，孑立捧奠，顧眄無後繼者，懍懍然欷歔惴惕，恐此事便已，摧心傷骨，若受鋒刃。

translations.literal: Each spring and autumn at the seasonal offerings I stand alone holding the sacrifice, looking around with no successor — fearful, sighing, apprehensive, dreading that this matter is already finished; it shatters heart and wounds bone, as if receiving a blade.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn at the seasonal offerings I stand alone holding the sacrifice, looking around with no successor — fearful, sighing, apprehensive, dreading that this matter is already finished; it shatters heart and wounds bone, as if receiving a blade.

sentences.zh: 此誠丈人所共閔惜也。

translations.literal: This is truly what you, Sir, would together pity and regret.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly what you, Sir, would together pity and regret.

sentences.zh: 先墓在城南，無異子弟為主，獨托村鄰。

translations.literal: The ancestral tombs are south of the city; no younger kinsmen serve as custodians — I rely alone on village neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral tombs are south of the city; no younger kinsmen serve as custodians — I rely alone on village neighbors.

sentences.zh: 自譴逐來，消息存亡不一至，鄉閭主守固以益怠。

translations.literal: Since my banishment, word of life and death has not come regularly; the village custodians have naturally grown ever more negligent.
translations.idiomatic: Since my banishment, word of life and death has not come regularly; the village custodians have naturally grown ever more negligent.

sentences.zh: 晝夜哀憤，懼便毀傷松柏，芻牧不禁，以成大戾。

translations.literal: Day and night I grieve and rage, fearing the pines and cypresses will soon be damaged, fodder and grazing unchecked, until a great violation is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night I grieve and rage, fearing the pines and cypresses will soon be damaged and fodder and grazing go unchecked until a great violation is complete.

sentences.zh: 近世禮重拜掃，今闕者四年矣。

translations.literal: In recent times ritual honors tomb-sweeping; I have now been absent four years.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times ritual honors tomb-sweeping; I have now been absent four years.

sentences.zh: 每遇寒食，則北向長號，以首頓地。

translations.literal: Each time Cold Food Festival comes, I wail long facing north, striking my head upon the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Each Cold Food Festival I wail long facing north, striking my head upon the ground.

sentences.zh: 想田野道路，士女遍滿，皁隸庸丐，皆得上父母丘墓；

translations.literal: I think of the fields and roads, gentlemen and ladies filling them everywhere; runners, servants, and common beggars all able to reach their parents' mounds;
translations.idiomatic: I think of the fields and roads, gentlemen and ladies filling them everywhere; runners, servants, and common beggars all able to reach their parents' mounds;

sentences.zh: 馬醫、夏畦之鬼，無不受子孫追養者。

translations.literal: the ghosts of horse doctors and summer field workers — none go without descendants to tend and nourish them.
translations.idiomatic: the ghosts of horse doctors and summer field workers — none go without descendants to tend and nourish them.

sentences.zh: 然此已息望，又何以雲哉？

translations.literal: Yet I have already ceased to hope for this — what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have already ceased to hope for this — what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 城西有數頃田，樹果數百株，多先人手自封植，今已荒穢，恐便斬伐，無復愛惜。

translations.literal: West of the city are several qing of fields and several hundred fruit trees, mostly planted by the forefathers' own hands; now they are overgrown and foul, and I fear they will soon be cut down with no further care.
translations.idiomatic: West of the city are several qing of fields and several hundred fruit trees, mostly planted by the forefathers' own hands. Now they are overgrown and foul, and I fear they will soon be cut down with no further care.

sentences.zh: 家有賜書三千卷，尚在善和裏舊宅，宅今三易主，書存亡不可知。

translations.literal: The family has three thousand volumes of granted books, still in the old house in Shanhe Lane; the house has now changed hands three times — whether the books survive cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: The family has three thousand volumes of granted books, still in the old house in Shanhe Lane. The house has now changed hands three times — whether the books survive cannot be known.

sentences.zh: 皆付受所重，常系心腑，然無可為者。

translations.literal: All were entrusted to what I valued; they constantly bind my heart — yet there is nothing to be done.
translations.idiomatic: All were entrusted to what I valued; they constantly bind my heart — yet there is nothing to be done.

sentences.zh: 立身一敗，萬事瓦裂，身殘家破，為世大僇。

translations.literal: One failure in establishing oneself, and ten thousand affairs shatter like tiles; body broken, family ruined — the world's great disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: One failure in establishing oneself, and ten thousand affairs shatter like tiles; body broken, family ruined — the world's great disgrace.

sentences.zh: 是以當食不知辛鹹節適，洗沐盥漱，動逾歲時，一搔皮膚，塵垢滿爪，誠憂恐悲傷，無所告訴，以至此也。

translations.literal: Thus when I eat I know neither salt nor savor nor measure; washing, bathing, rinsing, and brushing — each motion exceeds a year's time; one scratch of the skin and dust fills the nails — truly worry, fear, grief, and sorrow with none to tell, until it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when I eat I know neither salt nor savor; washing, bathing, and brushing — each motion exceeds a year's time; one scratch of the skin and dust fills the nails — truly worry, fear, grief, and sorrow with none to tell, until it has come to this.

sentences.zh: 自古賢人才士，秉志遵分，被謗議不能自明者，以百數。

translations.literal: From antiquity worthy men and talented scholars who held to their aims and kept their place yet were slandered and could not clear themselves number in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity worthy men and talented scholars who held to their aims yet were slandered and could not clear themselves number in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 故有無兄盜嫂，娶孤女撾婦翁者。

translations.literal: Thus there were those accused of seducing a sister-in-law without a brother, or marrying an orphan girl and beating her father-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Thus there were those accused of seducing a sister-in-law, or marrying an orphan girl and beating her father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 然賴當世豪傑分明辨列，卒光史冊。

translations.literal: Yet relying on the heroes of the age to distinguish and set forth clearly, they ultimately shine in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Yet relying on the heroes of the age to distinguish and set forth clearly, they ultimately shine in the historical records.

sentences.zh: 管仲遇盜，升為功臣；

translations.literal: Guan Zhong met with bandits and rose to become a meritorious minister;
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong met with bandits and rose to become a meritorious minister;

sentences.zh: 匡章被不孝名，孟子禮之。

translations.literal: Kuang Zhang bore the name of unfiliality, yet Mencius treated him with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Zhang bore the name of unfiliality, yet Mencius treated him with ritual.

sentences.zh: 今已無古人之實為而有詬，欲望世人之明己，不可得也。

translations.literal: Today there are no such deeds as the ancients had, yet there is slander — to hope the men of the world will understand oneself is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Today there are no such deeds as the ancients had, yet there is slander — to hope the men of the world will understand oneself is impossible.

sentences.zh: 直不疑買金以償同舍；

translations.literal: Zhi Buyi bought gold to repay a roommate;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Buyi bought gold to repay a roommate;

sentences.zh: 劉寬下車，歸牛鄉人。

translations.literal: Liu Kuan dismounted from his carriage and returned an ox to a villager.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuan dismounted from his carriage and returned an ox to a villager.

sentences.zh: 此誠知疑似之不可辯，非口舌所能勝也。

translations.literal: These truly knew that what seems doubtful cannot be argued, and that the tongue cannot prevail.
translations.idiomatic: These truly knew that what seems doubtful cannot be argued, and that the tongue cannot prevail.

sentences.zh: 鄭詹束縛于晉，終以無死；

translations.literal: Zheng Zhan was bound in Jin and in the end did not die;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhan was bound in Jin and in the end did not die;

sentences.zh: 鐘儀南音，卒獲返國；

translations.literal: Zhong Yi sang southern songs and ultimately returned to his state;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yi sang southern songs and ultimately returned to his state;

sentences.zh: 叔向囚虜，自期必免；

translations.literal: Shu Xiang was a captive prisoner yet expected he would surely be spared;
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xiang was a captive prisoner yet expected he would surely be spared;

sentences.zh: 范痤騎危，以生易死；

translations.literal: Fan Chuo rode in peril and traded life for death;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chuo rode in peril and traded life for death;

sentences.zh: 蒯通據鼎耳，為齊上客；

translations.literal: Kuai Tong grasped the cauldron's ears and became a honored guest of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Tong grasped the cauldron's ears and became an honored guest of Qi;

sentences.zh: 張蒼、韓信伏斧鑕，終取將相；

translations.literal: Zhang Cang and Han Xin submitted to the axe and block yet ultimately attained general and chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cang and Han Xin submitted to the axe and block yet ultimately attained general and chancellor;

sentences.zh: 鄒陽獄中，以書自治；

translations.literal: Zou Yang in prison cleared himself through writing;
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yang in prison cleared himself through writing;

sentences.zh: 賈生斥逐，復召宣室；

translations.literal: Master Jia was expelled and banished, then summoned again to the Xuan Room;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi was expelled and banished, then summoned again to the Xuan Room;

sentences.zh: 兒寬擯厄，後至御史大夫；

translations.literal: Er Kuan was cast out in hardship and later reached Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: Er Kuan was cast out in hardship and later reached Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 董仲舒、劉向下獄當誅，為漢儒宗。

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang entered prison deserving execution yet became the Confucian patriarchs of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang entered prison deserving execution yet became the Confucian patriarchs of Han.

sentences.zh: 此皆瑰偉博辯奇壯之士，能自解脫。

translations.literal: These were all magnificent, broad, eloquent, strange, and mighty men who could extricate themselves.
translations.idiomatic: These were all magnificent, broad, eloquent, and mighty men who could extricate themselves.

sentences.zh: 今以恇怯淟涊，下才末伎，又嬰痼病，雖欲慷慨攘臂，自同昔人，愈疏闊矣。

translations.literal: Now with timidity, servility, and sycophancy, low talent and petty skills, and again afflicted with chronic illness — though I wish to be bold and shake my arms, making myself like the men of old, I am only the more distant and estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Now with timidity, servility, and sycophancy, low talent and petty skills, and again afflicted with chronic illness — though I wish to be bold and shake my arms, making myself like the men of old, I am only the more distant and estranged.

sentences.zh: 賢者不得志於今，必取貴于後，古之著書者皆是也。

translations.literal: The worthy who do not achieve their aims in the present must take honor in later ages — all the ancients who wrote books were so.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy who do not achieve their aims in the present must take honor in later ages — all the ancients who wrote books were so.

sentences.zh: 宗元近欲務此，然力薄志劣，無異能解，欲秉筆覙縷，神志荒耗，前後遺忘，終不能成章。

translations.literal: Zongyuan lately wishes to devote himself to this, yet strength is thin and will inferior, with no special ability to explain; wishing to take up the brush and set forth in detail, spirit and mind are wasted and exhausted, forgetting before and after — in the end he cannot complete a piece.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan lately wishes to devote himself to this, yet strength is thin and will inferior, with no special ability to explain. Wishing to take up the brush and set forth in detail, spirit and mind are wasted and exhausted, forgetting before and after — in the end he cannot complete a piece.

sentences.zh: 往時讀書，自以不至牴滯，今皆頑然無復省錄。

translations.literal: Formerly when I read books I thought I did not reach obstruction and stagnation; now all is dull with no further recall.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when I read books I thought I did not stagnate; now all is dull with no further recall.

sentences.zh: 讀古人一傳，數紙後，則再三伸卷，復觀姓氏，旋又廢失。

translations.literal: Reading one ancient biography, after several pages I would repeatedly unroll the scroll and look again at the surname, then immediately forget again.
translations.idiomatic: Reading one ancient biography, after several pages I would repeatedly unroll the scroll and look again at the surname, then immediately forget again.

sentences.zh: 假令萬一除刑部囚籍，復為士列，亦不堪當世用矣！

translations.literal: Even if by some ten-thousandth chance my name were removed from the Ministry of Justice's prisoner register and I rejoined the ranks of gentlemen, I would still be unfit for use in the present age!
translations.idiomatic: Even if by some ten-thousandth chance my name were removed from the Ministry of Justice's prisoner register and I rejoined the ranks of gentlemen, I would still be unfit for use in the present age!

sentences.zh: 伏惟興哀於無用之地，垂德於不報之所，以通家宗祀為念，有可動心者操之勿失。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will raise pity in a place of no use, extend virtue where no repayment can be made, keeping in mind the ancestral sacrifices of our connected families — if anything can move the heart, grasp it and do not let it go.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope you will raise pity in a place of no use, extend virtue where no repayment can be made, keeping in mind the ancestral sacrifices of our connected families — if anything can move the heart, grasp it and do not let it go.

sentences.zh: 雖不敢望歸掃塋域，退托先人之廬，以盡餘齒，姑遂少北，益輕瘴癘，就婚娶，求胄嗣，有可付託，即冥然長辭，如得甘寢，無復恨矣！

translations.literal: Though I dare not hope to return and sweep the tombs, withdraw and rely on the forefathers' dwelling to spend my remaining years — at least permit me to move somewhat north, lighten the miasma somewhat, marry and seek an heir; if there is one to entrust, then I may take my long leave in darkness, as if granted sweet sleep, with no further regret!
translations.idiomatic: Though I dare not hope to return and sweep the tombs, withdraw and rely on the forefathers' dwelling to spend my remaining years — at least permit me to move somewhat north, lighten the miasma somewhat, marry and seek an heir. If there is one to entrust, then I may take my long leave in darkness, as if granted sweet sleep, with no further regret!

sentences.zh: 然眾畏其才高，懲刈復進，故無用力者。

translations.literal: Yet the multitude feared his lofty talent; warned by the cutting down of those restored to office, therefore no one exerted effort on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the multitude feared his lofty talent; warned by the cutting down of those restored to office, therefore no one exerted effort on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 宗元久汩振，其為文，思益深。

translations.literal: Zongyuan long stagnated in exile; in his writing, thought grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan long stagnated in exile; in his writing, thought grew ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 嘗著書一篇，號《貞符》，曰：

translations.literal: He once wrote a piece called "The True Talisman," saying:
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a piece called "The True Talisman," saying:

sentences.zh: 臣所貶州流人吳武陵為臣言：「董仲舒對三代受命之符，誠然？

translations.literal: The exiled man Wu Wuling in my banished prefecture said to me, "When Dong Zhongshu answered regarding the talismans of the Three Dynasties receiving the Mandate — was he right?
translations.idiomatic: The exiled man Wu Wuling in my banished prefecture said to me, "When Dong Zhongshu answered regarding the talismans of the Three Dynasties receiving the Mandate — was he right?

sentences.zh: 非邪？」

translations.literal: Or wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Or wrong?

sentences.zh: 臣曰：「非也。

translations.literal: I said, "Wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I said, "Wrong.

sentences.zh: 何獨仲舒爾，司馬相如、劉向、揚雄、班彪、彪子固皆沿襲嗤嗤，推古瑞物以配受命，其言類淫巫瞽史，誑亂後代，不足以知聖人立極之本，顯至德，揚大功，甚失厥趣。

translations.literal: Why only Zhongshu? Sima Xiangru, Liu Xiang, Yang Xiong, Ban Biao, and Biao's son Gu all followed along with snickering, pushing ancient auspicious objects to match receiving the Mandate — their words resemble debauched shamans and blind historians, deceiving and confusing later generations, insufficient to know the root of the sage establishing the pole, displaying supreme virtue, and raising great merit — greatly missing the point.
translations.idiomatic: Why only Zhongshu? Sima Xiangru, Liu Xiang, Yang Xiong, Ban Biao, and Biao's son Gu all followed along with snickering, pushing ancient auspicious objects to match receiving the Mandate — their words resemble debauched shamans and blind historians, deceiving and confusing later generations, insufficient to know the root of the sage establishing the pole, displaying supreme virtue, and raising great merit — greatly missing the point.

sentences.zh: 臣為尚書郎時，嘗著《貞符》，言唐家正德受命于生人之意、累積厚久宜享無極之義，本末閎闊。

translations.literal: When I was a Director in the Department of State Affairs, I once wrote "The True Talisman," speaking of the Tang house receiving the Mandate through upright virtue in accord with the people's will, and the meaning that accumulated thickness over long time should enjoy boundless blessing — root and branch broad and vast.
translations.idiomatic: When I was a Director in the Department of State Affairs, I once wrote "The True Talisman," speaking of the Tang house receiving the Mandate through upright virtue in accord with the people's will, and the meaning that accumulated thickness over long time should enjoy boundless blessing — root and branch broad and vast.

sentences.zh: 會貶逐中輟，不克備究。」

translations.literal: But in the midst of banishment it was interrupted and could not be fully completed.
translations.idiomatic: But in the midst of banishment it was interrupted and could not be fully completed.

sentences.zh: 武陵即叩頭邀臣：「此大事，不宜以辱故休缺，使聖王之典不立，無以抑詭類、拔正道、表核萬代。」

translations.literal: Wuling immediately kowtowed and urged me: "This is a great matter — it should not be left incomplete because of disgrace, lest the sage king's standard not be established, with no means to suppress the perverse, uplift the correct Way, and set the measure for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Wuling immediately kowtowed and urged me: "This is a great matter — it should not be left incomplete because of disgrace, lest the sage king's standard not be established, with no means to suppress the perverse, uplift the correct Way, and set the measure for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 臣不勝奮激，即具為書。

translations.literal: I could not restrain my ardor and immediately wrote it out in full.
translations.idiomatic: I could not restrain my ardor and immediately wrote it out in full.

sentences.zh: 念終泯沒蠻夷，不聞于時，獨不為也。

translations.literal: Reflecting that I would ultimately perish obscure among barbarians, unheard in my time — I alone could not allow that.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that I would ultimately perish obscure among barbarians, unheard in my time — I alone could not allow that.

sentences.zh: 苟一明大道，施于人世，死無所憾，用是自決。

translations.literal: If I might once clarify the great Way and apply it to the human world, I would die without regret — for this I resolved myself.
translations.idiomatic: If I might once clarify the great Way and apply it to the human world, I would die without regret — for this I resolved myself.

sentences.zh: 臣宗元稽首拜手以聞曰：

translations.literal: Your subject Zongyuan, bowing and clasping hands, reports and says:
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Zongyuan, bowing and clasping hands, reports and says:

sentences.zh: 孰稱古初，朴蒙空侗而無爭，厥流以訛，越乃奮奪，鬥怒振動，專肆為淫威？

translations.literal: Who says that in remote antiquity men were simple, blank, and empty, without strife — that only as the stream grew corrupt did they suddenly seize and wrest, fight in rage and tremble, and exclusively indulge in tyrannical power?
translations.idiomatic: Who says that in remote antiquity men were simple and without strife — that only as the stream grew corrupt did they suddenly seize power, fight in rage, and exclusively indulge in tyranny?

sentences.zh: 曰：是不知道。

translations.literal: I say: this is not knowing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: I say: this is not knowing the Way.

sentences.zh: 惟人之初，總總而生，林林而群。

translations.literal: At the beginning of mankind, they were born in multitudes and gathered in crowds.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of mankind, they were born in multitudes and gathered in crowds.

sentences.zh: 雪霜風雨雷雹暴其外，於是乃知架巢空穴，挽草木，取皮革；

translations.literal: Snow, frost, wind, rain, thunder, and hail assailed them from without; then they knew to build nests and hollow caves, pull grasses and trees, and take hides and leather;
translations.idiomatic: Snow, frost, wind, rain, thunder, and hail assailed them from without; then they knew to build nests and hollow caves, pull grasses and trees, and take hides and leather;

sentences.zh: 饑渴牝牡之欲驅其內，於是乃噬禽獸，咀果穀。

translations.literal: hunger, thirst, and male-female desire drove them from within; then they devoured birds and beasts and chewed fruits and grain.
translations.idiomatic: hunger, thirst, and desire drove them from within; then they devoured birds and beasts and chewed fruits and grain.

sentences.zh: 合偶而居，交焉而爭，睽焉而鬥，力大者搏，齒利者齧，爪剛者決，群眾者軋，兵良者殺，披披藉藉，草野塗血。

translations.literal: Pairing to dwell together, they mingled and quarreled, parted and fought — the strong grappled, the sharp-toothed bit, the hard-clawed tore, the numerous crushed, the well-armed killed; scattered and strewn, the wilds and fields were smeared with blood.
translations.idiomatic: Pairing to dwell together, they mingled and quarreled, parted and fought — the strong grappled, the sharp-toothed bit, the hard-clawed tore, the numerous crushed, the well-armed killed; scattered and strewn, the wilds and fields were smeared with blood.

sentences.zh: 在後強有力者出而治之，往往為曹于險陰，用號令起，而君臣什伍之法立。

translations.literal: Later the strong and powerful arose to govern them, often gathering bands in perilous places, raising themselves through commands, and establishing the laws of ruler and minister and the grouping of tens and fives.
translations.idiomatic: Later the strong and powerful arose to govern them, often gathering bands in perilous places, raising themselves through commands, and establishing the laws of ruler and minister and the grouping of tens and fives.

sentences.zh: 德紹者嗣，道怠者奪。

translations.literal: Those who inherited virtue succeeded; those who slackened in the Way were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who inherited virtue succeeded; those who slackened in the Way were removed.

sentences.zh: 於是有聖人焉，曰黃帝，游其兵車，交貫乎其內，一統類，齊制量，然猶大公之道不克建。

translations.literal: Then there was a sage named the Yellow Emperor, who deployed chariots of war and wove order throughout within, unifying categories and standardizing measures — yet still the great impartial Way could not be fully established.
translations.idiomatic: Then there was a sage named the Yellow Emperor, who deployed chariots of war and wove order throughout, unifying categories and standardizing measures — yet still the great impartial Way could not be fully established.

sentences.zh: 於是有聖人焉，曰堯，置州牧四嶽，持而綱之，立有德有功有能者，參而維之，運臂率指，屈伸把握，莫不統率；

translations.literal: Then there was a sage named Yao, who appointed regional governors and the Four Peaks, holding them as the net's cords, establishing men of virtue, merit, and ability to assist and sustain him — moving arm to lead finger, bending and extending, grasping and holding — nothing not governed;
translations.idiomatic: Then there was a sage named Yao, who appointed regional governors and the Four Peaks, holding them as the net's cords, establishing men of virtue, merit, and ability to assist and sustain him — moving arm to lead finger, bending and extending, grasping and holding — nothing not governed;

sentences.zh: 年老，舉聖人而禪焉，大公乃克建。

translations.literal: when old, he raised a sage and abdicated to him — then the great impartial Way could be established.
translations.idiomatic: when old, he raised a sage and abdicated to him — then the great impartial Way could be established.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，厥初罔匪極亂，而後稍可為也。

translations.literal: From this we see that at the beginning there was nothing but extreme disorder, and only afterward could things gradually be done.
translations.idiomatic: From this we see that at the beginning there was nothing but extreme disorder, and only afterward could things gradually be done.

sentences.zh: 而非德不樹，故仲尼敘《書》，於堯曰「克明俊德」，於舜曰「濬哲文明」，于禹曰「文命祗承於帝」，于湯曰「克寬克仁，章信兆民」，于武王曰「有道曾孫」。

translations.literal: Nothing is established without virtue; therefore Confucius arranged the Documents — of Yao he said "He was able to make bright his lofty virtue," of Shun "Deeply wise and civilly accomplished," of Yu "With cultured mandate reverently received from the Emperor," of Tang "Able in breadth and able in benevolence, making faith manifest to the myriad people," of King Wu "The worthy great-grandson."
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is established without virtue; therefore Confucius arranged the Documents — of Yao he said "He was able to make bright his lofty virtue," of Shun "Deeply wise and civilly accomplished," of Yu "With cultured mandate reverently received from the Emperor," of Tang "Able in breadth and able in benevolence, making faith manifest to the myriad people," of King Wu "The worthy great-grandson."

sentences.zh: 稽揆典誓，貞哉惟茲德，實受命之符，以奠永祀。

translations.literal: Examining the canonical oaths, steadfast is this virtue alone — it is truly the talisman of receiving the Mandate, to establish eternal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the canonical oaths, steadfast is this virtue alone — it is truly the talisman of receiving the Mandate, to establish eternal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 後之祅淫囂昏好怪之徒，乃始陳大電、大虹、玄鳥、巨跡、白狼、白魚、流火之烏以為符，斯皆詭譎闊誕，其可羞也，莫知本於厥貞。

translations.literal: Later the demonic, debauched, clamorous, dim, and strangeness-loving sort began to set forth great lightning, great rainbows, dark birds, giant footprints, white wolves, white fish, and fire-streaming birds as talismans — all bizarre, extravagant, and absurd, shameful things, not knowing that the root lies in this steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: Later the demonic, debauched, clamorous, and strangeness-loving sort began to set forth great lightning, great rainbows, dark birds, giant footprints, white wolves, white fish, and fire-streaming birds as talismans — all bizarre, extravagant, and absurd, shameful things, not knowing that the root lies in this steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 漢用大度，克懷於有氓，登能庸賢，濯痍煦寒，以瘳以熙，茲其為符也。

translations.literal: Han employed great magnanimity, able to embrace the people, elevating the capable and employing the worthy, washing wounds and warming the cold, healing and brightening — this was its talisman.
translations.idiomatic: Han employed great magnanimity, able to embrace the people, elevating the capable and employing the worthy, washing wounds and warming the cold, healing and brightening — this was its talisman.

sentences.zh: 而其妄臣，乃下取虺蛇，上引天光，推類號休，用誇誣於無知氓，增以騶虞、神鼎，脅驅縱踴，俾東之泰山、石閭，作大號謂之「封禪」，皆《尚書》所無有。

translations.literal: Yet its reckless ministers descended to take serpents, ascended to draw heavenly light, inferred categories and proclaimed blessings, using them to boast and deceive the ignorant people, adding the zouyu and divine cauldrons, coercing and driving them to leap and dance, sending them east to Mount Tai and Shilü, making a great title called "Feng and Shan" — all absent from the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Yet its reckless ministers descended to take serpents, ascended to draw heavenly light, inferred categories and proclaimed blessings, using them to boast and deceive the ignorant people, adding the zouyu and divine cauldrons, coercing and driving them to leap and dance, sending them east to Mount Tai and Shilü, making a great title called "Feng and Shan" — all absent from the Documents.

sentences.zh: 莽、述承效，卒奮驁逆。

translations.literal: Wang Mang and Gongsun Shu followed their example and ultimately rose in arrogant rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang and Gongsun Shu followed their example and ultimately rose in arrogant rebellion.

sentences.zh: 其後有賢帝曰光武，克綏天下，復承舊物，猶崇《赤伏》，以玷厥德。

translations.literal: Afterward there was a worthy emperor named Guangwu, who was able to pacify the realm and again inherit the old patrimony — yet still honored the "Red Talisman," tarnishing his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward there was a worthy emperor named Guangwu, who was able to pacify the realm and again inherit the old patrimony — yet still honored the "Red Talisman," tarnishing his virtue.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉而下，尨亂鉤裂，厥符不貞，邦用不靖，亦罔克久，駁乎無以議為也。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, confusion multiplied and hooks tore apart; their talismans were not steadfast, the state was not tranquil, and they also could not endure long — a tangle with nothing worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin downward, confusion multiplied and hooks tore apart; their talismans were not steadfast, the state was not tranquil, and they also could not endure long — a tangle with nothing worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 積大亂至於隋氏，環四海以為鼎，跨九垠以為爐，爨以毒燎，煽以虐焰，其人沸湧灼爛，號呼騰蹈，莫有救止。

translations.literal: Great disorder accumulated until the Sui house, which ringed the four seas as a cauldron and spanned the nine bounds as a furnace, cooking with poisonous flame and fanning with tyrannical fire — the people boiled, surged, burned, and scorched, crying out and leaping; none could rescue or stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Great disorder accumulated until the Sui house, which ringed the four seas as a cauldron and spanned the nine bounds as a furnace, cooking with poisonous flame and fanning with tyrannical fire — the people boiled, surged, burned, and scorched, crying out and leaping; none could rescue or stop it.

sentences.zh: 於是大聖乃起，丕降霖雨，濬滌蕩沃，蒸為清氛，疏為泠風，人乃漻然休然，相晞以生，相持以成，相彌以寧。

translations.literal: Then the great sage arose, greatly sending down rain, dredging, washing, flooding, and pouring — steaming into clear atmosphere, dispersing into cool wind — and people then became serene and at rest, moistening one another to live, supporting one another to complete, filling one another to find peace.
translations.idiomatic: Then the great sage arose, greatly sending down rain, dredging, washing, flooding, and pouring — steaming into clear atmosphere, dispersing into cool wind — and people then became serene and at rest, moistening one another to live, supporting one another to complete, filling one another to find peace.

sentences.zh: 琢斮屠剔膏流節離之禍不作，而人乃克完平舒愉，屍其肌膚，以達於夷途。

translations.literal: The calamities of carving, chopping, slaughtering, flaying, flowing fat, and severed joints did not arise, and people could then be whole, level, easy, and pleased, laying their flesh upon the level path.
translations.idiomatic: The calamities of carving, chopping, slaughtering, flaying, flowing fat, and severed joints did not arise, and people could then be whole, level, easy, and pleased, laying their flesh upon the level path.

sentences.zh: 焚坼抵掎奔走轉死之害不起，而人乃克鳩類集族，歌舞悅懌，用抵於元德。

translations.literal: The harms of burning, splitting, butting, running, and turning to death did not arise, and people could then gather kind and assemble clan, sing and dance in joy, reaching the primal virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The harms of burning, splitting, butting, running, and turning to death did not arise, and people could then gather kind and assemble clan, sing and dance in joy, reaching the primal virtue.

sentences.zh: 徒奮袒呼，犒迎義旅，歡動六合，至於麾下。

translations.literal: Bare-armed they strove and shouted, feasting and welcoming the army of righteousness; joy shook the six directions, reaching beneath his banners.
translations.idiomatic: Bare-armed they strove and shouted, feasting and welcoming the army of righteousness; joy shook the six directions, reaching beneath his banners.

sentences.zh: 大盜豪據，阻命遏德，義威殄戮，鹹墜厥緒。

translations.literal: Great robbers and proud usurpers blocked the Mandate and checked virtue; righteous might exterminated them, and all fell from their line.
translations.idiomatic: Great robbers and proud usurpers blocked the Mandate and checked virtue; righteous might exterminated them, and all fell from their line.

sentences.zh: 無劉於虐，人乃並受休嘉，去隋氏，克歸於唐，躑躅謳歌，灝灝和寧。

translations.literal: Without being cut down by tyranny, people together received blessing and grace, left the Sui house, and were able to return to Tang — halting and singing, vast and harmonious in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Without being cut down by tyranny, people together received blessing and grace, left the Sui house, and were able to return to Tang — halting and singing, vast and harmonious in peace.

sentences.zh: 帝庸威栗，惟人之為。

translations.literal: The emperor used awe and reverence — all for the sake of the people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor used awe and reverence — all for the sake of the people.

sentences.zh: 敬奠厥賦，積藏於下，是謂豐國。

translations.literal: Reverently setting forth their levies, storing accumulations below — this is called enriching the state.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently setting forth their levies, storing accumulations below — this is called enriching the state.

sentences.zh: 鄉為義廩，斂發謹飭，歲丁大侵，人以有年。

translations.literal: Districts established charity granaries, collecting and distributing with strict care; when years brought great famine, the people still had harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Districts established charity granaries, collecting and distributing with strict care; when years brought great famine, the people still had harvest.

sentences.zh: 簡于厥刑，不殘而懲，是謂嚴威。

translations.literal: Simplifying their punishments, chastising without mutilation — this is called stern awe.
translations.idiomatic: Simplifying their punishments, chastising without mutilation — this is called stern awe.

sentences.zh: 小屬而支，大生而孥，愷悌祗敬，用底於治。

translations.literal: Small clans were supported, great ones produced offspring; kind and respectful, they reached good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Small clans were supported, great ones produced offspring; kind and respectful, they reached good governance.

sentences.zh: 凡其所欲，不謁而獲；

translations.literal: Whatever they desired, they obtained without petition;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever they desired, they obtained without petition;

sentences.zh: 凡其所惡，不祈而息。

translations.literal: whatever they hated, ceased without prayer.
translations.idiomatic: whatever they hated, ceased without prayer.

sentences.zh: 四夷稽服，不作兵革，不竭貨力。

translations.literal: The four barbarians bowed in submission; no armies were raised, no goods or strength exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The four barbarians bowed in submission; no armies were raised, no goods or strength exhausted.

sentences.zh: 丕揚於後嗣，用垂於帝式，十聖濟厥治，孝仁平寬，惟祖之則。

translations.literal: Greatly exalted among later generations, handed down as the imperial model — ten sage emperors continued this governance: filial, benevolent, peaceful, and broad, following only the ancestors' example.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly exalted among later generations, handed down as the imperial model — ten sage emperors continued this governance: filial, benevolent, peaceful, and broad, following only the ancestors' example.

sentences.zh: 澤久而逾深，仁增而益高，人之戴唐，永永無窮。

translations.literal: Grace lasting long grew ever deeper; benevolence increased and rose ever higher — the people's support of Tang, forever without end.
translations.idiomatic: Grace lasting long grew ever deeper; benevolence increased and rose ever higher — the people's support of Tang, forever without end.

sentences.zh: 是故受命不于天，於其人；

translations.literal: Therefore receiving the Mandate is not from Heaven — it is from the people;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore receiving the Mandate is not from Heaven — it is from the people;

sentences.zh: 休符不于祥，於其仁。

translations.literal: the auspicious talisman is not in omens — it is in benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: the auspicious talisman is not in omens — it is in benevolence.

sentences.zh: 惟人之仁，匪祥於天。

translations.literal: Only the people's benevolence — no omen from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Only the people's benevolence — no omen from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 匪祥於天，茲惟貞符哉！

translations.literal: No omen from Heaven — this is the true talisman!
translations.idiomatic: No omen from Heaven — this is the true talisman!

sentences.zh: 未有喪仁而久者也，未有恃祥而壽者也。

translations.literal: Never has one who lost benevolence endured long; never has one who relied on omens lived long.
translations.idiomatic: Never has one who lost benevolence endured long; never has one who relied on omens lived long.

sentences.zh: 商之王以桑穀昌，以雉鴝大，宋之君以法星壽，鄭以龍衰，魯以麟弱，白雉亡漢，黃犀死莽，惡在其為符也？

translations.literal: The king of Shang prospered with mulberry and grain, grew great with pheasant and quail; the lord of Song lived long with the law star; Zheng declined with the dragon, Lu weakened with the unicorn; the white pheasant ended Han, the yellow rhinoceros killed Mang — where in these is the talisman?
translations.idiomatic: The king of Shang prospered with mulberry and grain, grew great with pheasant and quail; the lord of Song lived long with the law star; Zheng declined with the dragon, Lu weakened with the unicorn; the white pheasant ended Han, the yellow rhinoceros killed Mang — where in these is the talisman?

sentences.zh: 不勝唐德之代，光紹明濬，深鴻尨大，保人斯無疆，宜薦於郊廟，文之雅詩，祗告於德之休。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the age of Tang virtue — bright succession, clear depth, profound vastness and greatness, preserving the people without bound — it should be offered at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, written into the elegant odes, reverently announcing the blessing of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear the age of Tang virtue — bright succession, clear depth, profound vastness and greatness, preserving the people without bound — it should be offered at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, written into the elegant odes, reverently announcing the blessing of virtue.

sentences.zh: 帝曰諶哉！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "How sincere!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How sincere!"

sentences.zh: 乃黜休祥之奏，究貞符之奧，思德之所未大，求仁之所未備，以極於邦治，以敬於人事。

translations.literal: He then dismissed reports of auspicious omens, investigated the depths of the true talisman, considered where virtue had not yet grown great, sought where benevolence was not yet complete — to reach the utmost in governing the state and to be reverent in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismissed reports of auspicious omens, investigated the depths of the true talisman, considered where virtue had not yet grown great, sought where benevolence was not yet complete — to reach the utmost in governing the state and to be reverent in human affairs.

sentences.zh: 其詩曰：

translations.literal: The poem says:
translations.idiomatic: The poem says:

sentences.zh: 于穆敬德，黎人皇之。

translations.literal: Solemn and reverent in virtue — the people make it sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn and reverent in virtue — the people make it sovereign.

sentences.zh: 惟貞厥符，浩浩將之。

translations.literal: Only this steadfast talisman — vast, it will carry it forward.
translations.idiomatic: Only this steadfast talisman — vast, it will carry it forward.

sentences.zh: 仁函于膚，刃莫畢屠。

translations.literal: Benevolence enfolds the flesh — no blade can slaughter it all.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence enfolds the flesh — no blade can slaughter it all.

sentences.zh: 澤熯於爨，灊炎以澣。

translations.literal: Grace blazes at the hearth — hidden flame to wash away.
translations.idiomatic: Grace blazes at the hearth — hidden flame to wash away.

sentences.zh: 勃厥凶德，乃驅乃夷。

translations.literal: Violent evil virtue — drive it out and level it.
translations.idiomatic: Violent evil virtue — drive it out and level it.

sentences.zh: 懿其休風，是煦是吹。

translations.literal: Beautiful is this blessed wind — warm it and blow it.
translations.idiomatic: Beautiful is this blessed wind — warm it and blow it.

sentences.zh: 父子熙熙，相寧以嬉。

translations.literal: Fathers and sons joyful together, finding peace in play.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers and sons joyful together, finding peace in play.

sentences.zh: 賦徹而藏，厚我糗粻。

translations.literal: Levies collected and stored — enriching our grain and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Levies collected and stored — enriching our grain and provisions.

sentences.zh: 刑輕以清，我完靡傷。

translations.literal: Punishments light and clear — we are whole without harm.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments light and clear — we are whole without harm.

sentences.zh: 貽我子孫，百代是康。

translations.literal: Bequeathed to our sons and grandsons — a hundred generations of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Bequeathed to our sons and grandsons — a hundred generations of peace.

sentences.zh: 十聖嗣於治，仁后之子。

translations.literal: Ten sage emperors continue the governance — sons of the benevolent sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Ten sage emperors continue the governance — sons of the benevolent sovereign.

sentences.zh: 子思孝父，易患於己。

translations.literal: The son thinks of filial piety to the father, easily taking trouble upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: The son thinks of filial piety to the father, easily taking trouble upon himself.

sentences.zh: 拱之戴之，神其爾宜。

translations.literal: Revering and bearing it up — may the spirits approve you thus.
translations.idiomatic: Revering and bearing it up — may the spirits approve you thus.

sentences.zh: 載揚於雅，承天之嘏。

translations.literal: Carried forth in the elegant odes — receiving Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Carried forth in the elegant odes — receiving Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 天之誠神，宜鑒於仁。

translations.literal: Heaven's sincere spirit — should mirror itself in benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's sincere spirit — should mirror itself in benevolence.

sentences.zh: 神之曷依？

translations.literal: On what does the spirit rely?
translations.idiomatic: On what does the spirit rely?

sentences.zh: 宜仁之歸。

translations.literal: Benevolence is what it should return to.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence is what it should return to.

sentences.zh: 濮鈆于北，祝栗于南，幅員西東，祗一乃心。

translations.literal: Sacrifices at Pu to the north, prayers at Zhuli to the south — spanning west and east, reverently with one heart.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices at Pu to the north, prayers at Zhuli to the south — spanning west and east, reverently with one heart.

sentences.zh: 祝唐之紀，後天罔墜；

translations.literal: Pray for Tang's chronicle — may Heaven never fall;
translations.idiomatic: Pray for Tang's chronicle — may Heaven never fall;

sentences.zh: 祝皇之壽，與地咸久。

translations.literal: pray for the sovereign's longevity — with earth, enduring long.
translations.idiomatic: pray for the sovereign's longevity — with earth, enduring long.

sentences.zh: 曷徒祝之，心誠篤之。

translations.literal: Why merely pray? — let the heart be sincerely devoted.
translations.idiomatic: Why merely pray? — let the heart be sincerely devoted.

sentences.zh: 神協人同，道以告之。

translations.literal: Spirit and people in accord — the Way announces it.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit and people in accord — the Way announces it.

sentences.zh: 俾彌億萬年，不震不危。

translations.literal: May it extend ten thousand myriad years — unshaken, unendangered.
translations.idiomatic: May it extend ten thousand myriad years — unshaken, unendangered.

sentences.zh: 我代之延，永永毘之。

translations.literal: Our dynasty extended — forever joined to it.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty extended — forever joined to it.

sentences.zh: 仁增以崇，曷不爾思？

translations.literal: Benevolence increased and exalted — why do you not think on this?
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence increased and exalted — why do you not think on this?

sentences.zh: 有號於天，僉曰嗚呼，咨爾皇靈，無替厥符！

translations.literal: A cry to Heaven — all say "Alas!" Consult you, imperial spirit — do not replace this talisman!
translations.idiomatic: A cry to Heaven — all say "Alas!" Consult you, imperial spirit — do not replace this talisman!

sentences.zh: 宗元不得召，內閔悼，悔念往吝，作賦自儆曰：

translations.literal: Zongyuan was not recalled; inwardly grieving and lamenting, regretting and recalling past faults, he wrote a fu to warn himself, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan was not recalled; inwardly grieving and lamenting, regretting past faults, he wrote a fu to warn himself, saying:

sentences.zh: 懲咎愆以本始兮，孰非餘心之所求？

translations.literal: Punishing guilt from the root beginning — was this not what my heart sought?
translations.idiomatic: Punishing guilt from the root beginning — was this not what my heart sought?

sentences.zh: 處卑污以閔世兮，固前志之為尤。

translations.literal: Dwelling in lowliness and filth to pity the age — this was indeed the fault of my former resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in lowliness and filth to pity the age — this was indeed the fault of my former resolve.

sentences.zh: 始余學而觀古兮，怪今昔之異謀。

translations.literal: At first I studied and observed antiquity, marveling at how present and past differed in design.
translations.idiomatic: At first I studied and observed antiquity, marveling at how present and past differed in design.

sentences.zh: 惟聰明為可考兮，追駿步而遐遊。

translations.literal: Only the wise and clear could be examined — I pursued swift steps and traveled far.
translations.idiomatic: Only the wise and clear could be examined — I pursued swift steps and traveled far.

sentences.zh: 絜誠之既信直兮，仁友藹而萃之。

translations.literal: Pure sincerity, faithful and upright — benevolent friends gathered kindly around me.
translations.idiomatic: Pure sincerity, faithful and upright — benevolent friends gathered kindly around me.

sentences.zh: 日施陳以系縻兮，邀堯舜禹之為。

translations.literal: Daily I set forth and arranged, binding myself — inviting the deeds of Yao, Shun, and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Daily I set forth and arranged, binding myself — inviting the deeds of Yao, Shun, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 上睢盱而混茫兮，下駁詭而懷私。

translations.literal: Above, eyes wide and vision blurred; below, perverse and strange, harboring private aims.
translations.idiomatic: Above, eyes wide and vision blurred; below, perverse and strange, harboring private aims.

sentences.zh: 旁羅列以交貫兮，求大中之所宜。

translations.literal: On every side I arrayed and cross-linked, seeking what the great Mean approves.
translations.idiomatic: On every side I arrayed and cross-linked, seeking what the great Mean approves.

sentences.zh: 曰道有象兮，而無其形。

translations.literal: I said: the Way has images, yet no form of its own.
translations.idiomatic: I said: the Way has images, yet no form of its own.

sentences.zh: 推變乘時兮，與志相迎。

translations.literal: Infer change and seize the season — meet one's will in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Infer change and seize the season — meet one's will in accord.

sentences.zh: 不及則殆兮，過則失貞。

translations.literal: Falling short brings peril; going too far loses steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: Falling short brings peril; going too far loses steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 謹守而中兮，與時偕行。

translations.literal: Guard carefully and hold the center — walk in step with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Guard carefully and hold the center — walk in step with the times.

sentences.zh: 萬類芸芸兮，率由以寧。

translations.literal: The myriad kinds teem abundantly — all thereby find peace.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad kinds teem abundantly — all thereby find peace.

sentences.zh: 剛柔弛張兮，出入綸經。

translations.literal: Hard and soft, slack and taut — entering and leaving the warp and woof.
translations.idiomatic: Hard and soft, slack and taut — entering and leaving the warp and woof.

sentences.zh: 登能抑枉兮，白黑濁清。

translations.literal: Elevate the capable, restrain the crooked — white and black, turbid and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Elevate the capable, restrain the crooked — white and black, turbid and clear.

sentences.zh: 蹈乎大方兮，物莫能嬰。

translations.literal: Tread the great square — nothing can touch or harm.
translations.idiomatic: Tread the great square — nothing can touch or harm.

sentences.zh: 奉訏謨以植內兮，欣餘志之有獲。

translations.literal: Upholding far-reaching plans to plant them within, I rejoiced that my will had gain.
translations.idiomatic: Upholding far-reaching plans to plant them within, I rejoiced that my will had gain.

sentences.zh: 再明信乎策書兮，謂耿然而不惑。

translations.literal: Again and again I made clear my faith in policy documents, thinking myself bright and undeluded.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again I made clear my faith in policy documents, thinking myself bright and undeluded.

sentences.zh: 愚者果于自用兮，惟懼夫誠之不一。

translations.literal: The fool is resolute in self-will — I only feared that sincerity was not one.
translations.idiomatic: The fool is resolute in self-will — I only feared that sincerity was not one.

sentences.zh: 不顧慮以周圖兮，專茲道以為服。

translations.literal: Without looking ahead to plan comprehensively, I devoted this Way alone as my garment.
translations.idiomatic: Without looking ahead to plan comprehensively, I devoted this Way alone as my garment.

sentences.zh: 讒妒構而不戒兮，猶斷斷於所執。

translations.literal: Slander and envy plotted without warning — yet I still obstinately held to what I clung to.
translations.idiomatic: Slander and envy plotted without warning — yet I still obstinately held to my course.

sentences.zh: 哀吾黨之不淑兮，遭任遇之卒迫。

translations.literal: Alas, my faction was not good — we met appointment and encounter in sudden urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, my faction was not good — we met appointment and encounter in sudden crisis.

sentences.zh: 勢危疑而多詐兮，逢天地之否隔。

translations.literal: The situation was perilous and doubtful, with much deceit — we encountered the blockage of heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: The situation was perilous and doubtful, rife with deceit — we encountered the blockage of heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 欲圖退而保己兮，悼乖期乎曩昔。

translations.literal: Wishing to plan retreat and preserve myself, I mourned the broken promise of former days.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to retreat and preserve myself, I mourned the broken promise of former days.

sentences.zh: 欲操術以致忠兮，眾呀然而互嚇。

translations.literal: Wishing to wield methods to achieve loyalty, the multitude gaped and mutually frightened one another.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to wield methods to achieve loyalty, the multitude gaped and mutually frightened one another.

sentences.zh: 進與退吾無歸兮，甘脂潤兮鼎鑊。

translations.literal: Advancing or retreating, I had no return — I would gladly accept fat and grease in the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing or retreating, I had no return — I would gladly accept the cauldron's fate.

sentences.zh: 幸皇鑒之明宥兮，累郡印而南適。

translations.literal: Fortunate in the emperor's clear pardon, I accumulated prefectural seals and went south.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate in the emperor's clear pardon, I accumulated prefectural seals and went south.

sentences.zh: 惟罪大而寵厚兮，宜夫重仍乎禍謫。

translations.literal: Though guilt was great, favor was thick — it was fitting that calamity and banishment should come again.
translations.idiomatic: Though guilt was great, favor had been thick — it was fitting that calamity and banishment should come again.

sentences.zh: 既明懼乎天討兮，又幽慄乎鬼責。

translations.literal: Already clearly fearing Heaven's punishment, I was also darkly apprehensive of the ghosts' blame.
translations.idiomatic: Already clearly fearing Heaven's punishment, I was also darkly apprehensive of the ghosts' blame.

sentences.zh: 惶惶乎夜寤而晝駭兮，類鹿濩秬之不息。

translations.literal: Fearful — waking at night and startled by day, like a deer in panic that cannot rest.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful — waking at night and startled by day, like a deer in panic that cannot rest.

sentences.zh: 淩洞庭之洋洋兮，溯湘流之沄沄。

translations.literal: Crossing vast Dongting, I traced upstream the surging Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing vast Dongting, I traced upstream the surging Xiang.

sentences.zh: 飄風擊以揚波兮，舟摧抑而回邅。

translations.literal: Whirling wind struck and raised waves — the boat was battered and turned back in delay.
translations.idiomatic: Whirling wind struck and raised waves — the boat was battered and turned back.

sentences.zh: 日霾曀以昧幽兮，黝雲湧而上屯。

translations.literal: The sun was hazy and dim with gloom — dark clouds surged and piled above.
translations.idiomatic: The sun was hazy and dim — dark clouds surged and piled above.

sentences.zh: 暮屑窣以淫雨兮，聽嗷嗷之哀猿。

translations.literal: At dusk, pattering in drenching rain, I heard the wailing of mournful gibbons.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk, in drenching rain, I heard the wailing of mournful gibbons.

sentences.zh: 眾鳥萃而啾號兮，沸洲渚以連山。

translations.literal: Birds gathered and chirped and cried — islets seethed, linking with the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Birds gathered and cried — islets seethed, linking with the mountains.

sentences.zh: 漂遙逐其詎止兮，逝莫屬餘之形魂。

translations.literal: Drifting far, chasing where it would stop — departing, none attended my body and soul.
translations.idiomatic: Drifting far, chasing an unknown end — departing, none attended my body and soul.

sentences.zh: 攢巒奔以紆委兮，束洶湧之崩湍。

translations.literal: Massed peaks rushed in winding descent, binding the surging, crashing torrent.
translations.idiomatic: Massed peaks rushed in winding descent, binding the surging, crashing torrent.

sentences.zh: 畔尺進而尋退兮，蕩洄汩乎淪漣。

translations.literal: A foot's advance, then a yard's retreat — swirling, eddying, sinking in ripples.
translations.idiomatic: A foot's advance, then a yard's retreat — swirling and eddying in ripples.

sentences.zh: 際窮冬而止居兮，羈累棼以縈纏。

translations.literal: At the edge of deep winter I halted my dwelling — bonds and troubles tangled and wound around me.
translations.idiomatic: At deep winter I halted my dwelling — bonds and troubles tangled and wound around me.

sentences.zh: 哀吾生之孔艱兮，循《凱風》之悲詩。

translations.literal: Alas, how hard my life — following the sorrowful poem of the "Balmy Wind."
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how hard my life — following the sorrowful poem of the "Balmy Wind."

sentences.zh: 罪通天而降酷兮，不亟死而生為！

translations.literal: Guilt reached Heaven and brought down severity — why not die quickly rather than live on!
translations.idiomatic: Guilt reached Heaven and brought down severity — why not die quickly rather than live on!

sentences.zh: 逾再歲之寒暑兮，猶貿貿而自持。

translations.literal: Past two years of cold and heat, I still stubbornly held myself together.
translations.idiomatic: Past two years of cold and heat, I still stubbornly held myself together.

sentences.zh: 將沈淵而隕命兮，詎蔽罪以塞禍？

translations.literal: About to sink into the abyss and lose my life — how could hiding guilt block calamity?
translations.idiomatic: About to sink into the abyss and lose my life — how could hiding guilt block calamity?

sentences.zh: 惟滅身而無後兮，顧前志猶未可。

translations.literal: Only to destroy the body and leave no heir — yet looking back, my former resolve still could not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Only to destroy the body and leave no heir — yet my former resolve still could not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 進路呀以劃絕兮，退伏匿又不果。

translations.literal: The forward path gaped and was cut off; retreating to hide also could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The forward path gaped and was cut off; retreating to hide also could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 為孤囚以終世兮，長拘攣而轗軻。

translations.literal: A lonely prisoner for life — long cramped and stumbling on hardship.
translations.idiomatic: A lonely prisoner for life — long cramped and stumbling through hardship.

sentences.zh: 曩余志之脩蹇兮，今何為此戾也？

translations.literal: Formerly my will was lofty and arduous — why now have I come to this perversity?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly my will was lofty and arduous — why now have I come to this perversity?

sentences.zh: 豈貪食而盜名兮，不混同於世也。

translations.literal: Was it from greedy eating and stealing fame that I would not blend with the world?
translations.idiomatic: Was it from greedy eating and stealing fame that I would not blend with the world?

sentences.zh: 將顯身以直遂兮，眾之所宜蔽也。

translations.literal: Wishing to show myself and go straight through — this is what the multitude should have concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to show myself and go straight through — this is what the multitude should have concealed.

sentences.zh: 不擇言以危肆兮，固群禍之際也。

translations.literal: Not choosing words but speaking recklessly in peril — this was indeed the threshold of collective calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Not choosing words but speaking recklessly — this was indeed the threshold of collective calamity.

sentences.zh: 禦長轅之無橈兮，行九折之峨峨。

translations.literal: Driving the long yoke without a rudder, traveling the nine bends, steep and towering.
translations.idiomatic: Driving the long yoke without a rudder, traveling the nine steep bends.

sentences.zh: 卻驚棹以橫江兮，溯淩天之騰波。

translations.literal: Turning back the startled oar to cross the river, I traced sky-soaring surging waves upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Turning back the startled oar to cross the river, I traced sky-soaring waves upstream.

sentences.zh: 幸餘死之已緩兮，完形軀之既多。

translations.literal: Fortunate that my death has been delayed — my whole body yet largely intact.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate that my death has been delayed — my body yet largely intact.

sentences.zh: 苟餘齒之有懲兮，蹈前烈而不頗。

translations.literal: If my remaining years have warning, I will tread the former exemplars without deviation.
translations.idiomatic: If my remaining years hold warning, I will tread the former exemplars without deviation.

sentences.zh: 死蠻夷固吾所兮，雖顯寵其焉加？

translations.literal: To die among barbarians is indeed my portion — what could conspicuous favor add?
translations.idiomatic: To die among barbarians is indeed my portion — what could conspicuous favor add?

sentences.zh: 配大中以為偶兮，諒天命之謂何！

translations.literal: Matching the great Mean as my counterpart — I trust what Heaven's mandate must mean!
translations.idiomatic: Matching the great Mean as my counterpart — I trust what Heaven's mandate must mean!

sentences.zh: 元和十年，徙柳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe he was transferred to Prefect of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanhe he was transferred to Prefect of Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時劉禹錫得播州，宗元曰：「播非人所居，而禹錫親在堂，吾不忍其窮，無辭以白其大人，如不往，便為母子永決。」

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yuxi was assigned Bozhou; Zongyuan said, "Bo is no place for humans, and Yuxi's parent is still living. I cannot bear his hardship — I have no words to explain to his elders; if he does not go, it will be an eternal parting of mother and son.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Yuxi was assigned Bozhou; Zongyuan said, "Bo is no place for humans, and Yuxi's parent is still living. I cannot bear his hardship — I have no words to explain to his elders; if he does not go, it will be an eternal parting of mother and son.

sentences.zh: 即具奏欲以柳州授禹錫而自往播。

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a full memorial wishing to give Liuzhou to Yuxi and go himself to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a memorial wishing to give Liuzhou to Yuxi and go himself to Bo.

sentences.zh: 會大臣亦為禹錫請，因改連州。

translations.literal: It happened that great ministers also pleaded for Yuxi, so the assignment was changed to Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers also pleaded for Yuxi, so the assignment was changed to Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 柳人以男女質錢，過期不贖，子本均，則沒為奴婢。

translations.literal: The people of Liuzhou pledged men and women for loans; if they did not redeem them when due and principal and interest were equal, they were confiscated as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Liuzhou pledged men and women for loans; if they did not redeem them when due and principal and interest were equal, they were confiscated as slaves.

sentences.zh: 宗元設方計，悉贖歸之。

translations.literal: Zongyuan devised measures and redeemed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan devised measures and redeemed them all.

sentences.zh: 尤貧者，令書庸，視直足相當，還其質。

translations.literal: For the extremely poor, he had them record labor hire; when the value was sufficient, he returned their pledge.
translations.idiomatic: For the extremely poor, he had them record labor hire; when the value was sufficient, he returned their pledge.

sentences.zh: 已沒者，出己錢助贖。

translations.literal: Those already confiscated — he paid from his own funds to help redeem them.
translations.idiomatic: Those already confiscated — he paid from his own funds to help redeem them.

sentences.zh: 南方為進士者，走數千里從宗元遊，經指授者，為文辭皆有法。

translations.literal: Jinshi candidates from the south traveled thousands of li to study with Zongyuan; those he instructed in writing all produced prose with proper method.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi candidates from the south traveled thousands of li to study with Zongyuan; those he instructed all produced prose with proper method.

sentences.zh: 世號「柳柳州」。

translations.literal: The age called him "Liu of Liuzhou."
translations.idiomatic: The age called him "Liu of Liuzhou."

sentences.zh: 十四年卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died, aged forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 宗元少時嗜進，謂功業可就。

translations.literal: In youth Zongyuan was eager for advancement and thought great achievements could be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zongyuan was eager for advancement and thought great achievements lay within reach.

sentences.zh: 既坐廢，遂不振。

translations.literal: Once cast aside, he did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: Once cast aside, he did not recover.

sentences.zh: 然其才實高，名蓋一時。

translations.literal: Yet his talent was truly lofty and his fame covered the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his talent was truly lofty and his fame covered the age.

sentences.zh: 韓愈評其文曰：「雄深雅健，似司馬子長，崔、蔡不足多也。」

translations.literal: Han Yu appraised his writing: "Bold, deep, elegant, and strong — like Sima Qian; Cui and Cai are not worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu appraised his writing: "Bold, deep, elegant, and strong — like Sima Qian; Cui and Cai are not worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 既沒，柳人懷之，托言降於州之堂，人有慢者輒死。

translations.literal: After his death the people of Liuzhou cherished him, claiming he descended to the prefectural hall; those who showed disrespect died.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the people of Liuzhou cherished him, claiming he descended to the prefectural hall; those who showed disrespect died.

sentences.zh: 廟于羅池，愈因碑以實之云。

translations.literal: They enshrined him at Luochi Pool; Han Yu verified this with a stele.
translations.idiomatic: They enshrined him at Luochi Pool; Han Yu verified this with a stele.

sentences.zh: 程异，字師舉，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi, courtesy name Shiju, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi, courtesy name Shiju, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 居鄉以孝稱。

translations.literal: In his home district he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: In his home district he was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 第明經，再補鄭尉。

translations.literal: He passed the mingjing examination and twice served as assistant magistrate of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the mingjing examination and twice served as assistant magistrate of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 精吏治，為叔文所引，由監察御史為鹽鐵揚子院留後。

translations.literal: Skilled in administration, he was brought in by Shuwen and rose from Investigating Censor to acting head of the Yangzi Salt and Iron Office.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in administration, he was brought in by Shuwen and rose from Investigating Censor to acting head of the Yangzi Salt and Iron Office.

sentences.zh: 叔文敗，貶郴州司馬。

translations.literal: When Shuwen fell, Yi was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuwen fell, Yi was demoted to Prefectural Adjutant of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 李巽領鹽鐵，薦异心計可任，請拔擢用之，乃授侍御史，復為揚子留後。

translations.literal: Li Xun headed Salt and Iron, recommended Yi's schemes as reliable, and asked that he be promoted and employed; Yi was then appointed Attending Censor and again made acting head of the Yangzi office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun headed Salt and Iron, recommended Yi's schemes as reliable, and asked that he be promoted; Yi was then appointed Attending Censor and again made acting head of the Yangzi office.

sentences.zh: 稍遷淮南等道兩稅使。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Commissioner of the Two Tax Levies for Huainan and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually transferred to Commissioner of the Two Tax Levies for Huainan and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 异起退廢，能厲己竭節，悉矯革征利舊弊。

translations.literal: Yi rose from dismissal and disgrace, able to discipline himself and exhaust his integrity, thoroughly correcting old abuses in revenue extraction.
translations.idiomatic: Yi rose from dismissal and disgrace, able to discipline himself and exhaust his integrity, thoroughly correcting old abuses in revenue extraction.

sentences.zh: 入遷累衛尉卿、鹽鐵轉運副使。

translations.literal: He entered court and was promoted in succession to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court and was promoted in succession to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport.

sentences.zh: 方討蔡，异使江表調財用，因行諭諸帥府，以羨贏貢。

translations.literal: While Cai was being suppressed, Yi was sent to the lower Yangzi region to adjust finances; traveling, he instructed the military headquarters to submit surplus revenue as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: While Cai was being suppressed, Yi was sent to the lower Yangzi region to adjust finances; traveling, he instructed the military headquarters to submit surplus revenue as tribute.

sentences.zh: 故异所至，不剝下，不加斂，經用以饒。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever Yi went, he did not strip the people below or add levies — routine expenses were ample.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore wherever Yi went, he did not strip the people or add levies — routine expenses were ample.

sentences.zh: 遂兼御史大夫為鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: He then additionally served as Censor-in-Chief and Commissioner of Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: He then additionally served as Censor-in-Chief and Commissioner of Salt and Iron.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，以工部侍郎同中書門下平章事，猶領鹽鐵。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Chancellor, still heading Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Chancellor, still heading Salt and Iron.

sentences.zh: 异以錢穀奮而至宰相，自以非人望，久不敢當印秉筆。

translations.literal: Yi had risen through finance to chancellor; believing himself not the people's hope, for long he dared not take the seal and wield the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had risen through finance to chancellor; believing himself not the people's hope, for long he dared not take the seal and wield the brush.

sentences.zh: 明年，西北軍政不治，議置巡邊使，憲宗問孰可者，乃自請行。

translations.literal: The next year, military affairs in the northwest were poorly governed; when discussion arose of appointing a frontier inspector and Xianzong asked who could serve, Yi volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, military affairs in the northwest were poorly governed; when discussion arose of appointing a frontier inspector and Xianzong asked who could serve, Yi volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 會卒，贈尚書左僕射，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He happened to die and was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 身歿官第，無留貲，世重其廉雲。

translations.literal: He died in his official residence without retained wealth; the age honored his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his official residence without retained wealth; the age honored his integrity.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：叔文沾沾小人，竊天下柄，與陽虎取大弓《春秋》書為盜無以異。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: Shuwen was a fawning petty man who stole the handle of the realm — no different from Yang Hu taking the great bow, which the Spring and Autumn Annals records as theft.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist says: Shuwen was a fawning petty man who stole the handle of the realm — no different from Yang Hu taking the great bow, which the Spring and Autumn Annals records as theft.

sentences.zh: 宗元等橈節從之，徼幸一時，貪帝病昏，抑太子之明，規權遂私。

translations.literal: Zongyuan and the rest bent principle to follow him, hoping for luck in the moment, greedy while the emperor was ill and dim, suppressing the crown prince's clarity, plotting power to serve private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan and the rest bent principle to follow him, hoping for luck in the moment, greedy while the emperor was ill and dim, suppressing the crown prince's clarity, plotting power to serve private ends.

sentences.zh: 故賢者疾，不肖者媢，一僨而不復，宜哉！

translations.literal: Therefore the worthy were disgusted and the unworthy jealous — one fall and no recovery; it was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the worthy were disgusted and the unworthy jealous — one fall and no recovery; it was fitting!

sentences.zh: 彼若不傅匪人，自勵材猷，不失為明卿才大夫，惜哉！

translations.literal: Had they not attached themselves to unworthy men but encouraged their own talent and plans, they would not have failed to be enlightened ministers and talented grandees — what a pity!
translations.idiomatic: Had they not attached themselves to unworthy men but encouraged their own talent and plans, they would not have failed to be enlightened ministers and talented grandees — what a pity!
